$comment: easl API method catalog. Single source of truth for the socket protocol; clients (TS, Python, CLI) are generated from this file by scripts/gen-clients.ts. Bump `version` on any breaking change.

transport.framing: newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, UTF-8
transport.request: { id: string, method: string, params: object }
transport.response: { id: string, ok: true, result: any } | { id: string, ok: false, error: { code: string, message: string, data?: any } }
transport.events: after a successful events.subscribe, the same connection receives { event: string, data: any } lines until closed
transport.clients: after a successful client.attach the server also writes requests to that connection, { id: string, method: string, params: object } with ids "easld-<n>", for the methods the client serves; the client answers each with a response line carrying its id, in any order. A line from the client with `ok` and no `method` is such an answer. Relayed surface.stream calls also carry surfaceEvents: string[] outside params, the opening viewer's private-event subscriptions. Drawing clients push {event, board, data} surface events on that same attached link, with event encoded first; easld forwards them only to the stream's owning viewer

errors.not_found: referenced object, mention, agent, or authorized host file does not exist
errors.refused: host file request is outside its board-image authorization policy
errors.too_large: host image file exceeds the 4194304-byte board-image limit
errors.unreadable: authorized host file cannot be read, changed during its descriptor read, or contains invalid PNG/JPEG raster data
errors.conflict: rev mismatch on update; re-read and retry
errors.unsupported: method known but not implemented by this build
errors.unavailable: target exists but cannot act right now (e.g. a terminal tile without an attached surface), or the app is not running: no attached client (client.attach) serves the call, it didn't answer in time, or it disconnected before answering
errors.timeout: agent.wait or browser.wait deadline passed before the requested state
errors.ambiguous: an address (a terminal's name, `name@board`, a board's name, `board.open_remote`'s host name) matches more than one terminal, open board or host; the message lists each candidate (a terminal as `name@board (tile id)`, a host by its ssh target), so the caller can name one

root.description: Lexically normalized request board root, matching HostFiles metadata.

stamp.description: dev:ino:size:mtime_ns:ctime_ns from the stable descriptor used to read the bytes.

data.description: Alpha-preserving PNG bytes, smaller than the original file.

ViewerId.description: A remote window's in-memory identity, retained across reconnects and scoped to that window's edits and composer returns.

session.description: Live remote connection or stream identity.

receipt.description: Stable outcome identity; the same receipt appears live and in board.get so a viewer applies it once.

ids.description: Original staged mention ids, never copied delivery ids or captured targets.

raisedAt.description: The marker's identity for a guarded view.seen acknowledgment; echo the value from board.get or attention.changed.

step.description: The viewer's step that was replayed; omitted when no host history remains.

pushed.description: The replay created an opposite-stack step. The viewer uses this authoritative receipt even when repeating a command whose reply was lost.

retired.description: True when this non-live request's outcome receipt was retired. No changes are replayed; older live history is retained. Omitted otherwise.

kept.description: Objects with fields left unchanged because another edit replaced them.

SurfaceStream.description: A session owned only by the connection that opened it; never transferable between connections or reconnected clients.

SurfaceSize.description: Host WKWebView bounds in points, top-left origin. Input uses these points, not CSS pixels or encoded image pixels.

SurfaceInputEvent.description: Closed native-input union. Positive seq values increase strictly within each batch. Previously accepted seq values are ignored; callers never automatically resend input after reconnect. Raw mods are NSEvent modifier flags. Context menus are viewer-local.

text.description: Explicit paste payload; never mutates the host clipboard.

input.description: Conservative host app-queue watermark. Pending mouse/key processing checks hold it back until confirmed, and missing checks leave it unconfirmed. Direct text, scroll and commands have no WebKit processing check; this field does not guarantee their effects are visible in the image.

refresh.description: High-quality H264 refresh in the continuing video reference chain. Input can supersede it, forcing the next video frame to start with an independent keyframe.

supersedes.description: First sequence in a consecutive range of canceled refreshes ending immediately before this frame. The next H264 frame resets prediction with an independent keyframe. Published motion frames cannot be skipped.

canvas.description: Original raster dimensions. Native-size H264 rounds each dimension up to an even number with a minimum of 16, pads the bottom and right edges, and crops decoded output to this canvas.

offset.description: Refresh transport chunk byte offset. Only with refresh=true, format=h264 and total. The first chunk starts at zero; chunks are ordered.

total.description: Whole encoded refresh size. Each chunk contains exactly min(16384,total-offset) decoded bytes, with constant frame metadata.

SurfaceFrame.description: Private in-memory surface frame. JPEG and explicit PNG retain full images up to 16 MiB. Native h264 streams measure the first three decoded motion acknowledgements, then use one full-size quality-0.8 JPEG encode on fast links or bounded predicted ESV1 video on constrained links, regardless of topology. H264 motion is bounded to 48 KiB. After one second without input or a change to more than 1% of consecutive-capture pixels, a stream may send one native-size high-quality H264 refresh bounded to 576 KiB. Small later changes predict from that sharp reference. Large active input resumes warm motion with an independent keyframe. Periodic keyframe scheduling is disabled. Every sharp IDR uses refresh transport and never retries at motion quality. Cumulative changes beyond 1% rearm settling. Real-page RGB gates are in docs/testing.md. Refresh uses ordered 16 KiB chunks with one outstanding chunk. Each validated surface.progress receipt releases at most one next chunk, never frame credit. Chunks share one frame sequence and metadata and assemble into one complete ESV1 packet before decoding. They are not images or pixel regions. surface.ack follows complete decode and presentation. Input cancels refresh without waiting. The next frame declares the canceled range and independently resets prediction. Source writers skip untouched canceled refresh lines. Easld removes only queued same-board and same-stream refresh chunks in that range. Partial lines finish intact. No published motion reference is skipped. Decode failure or any other sequence gap requires a fresh stream without input replay.

modified.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

SurfaceFile.description: A viewer-picked file held only in memory. All files in one answer total at most 8 MiB decoded, including empty files. No viewer path or drawing-machine staging file is sent.

accept.description: File picker type hints from the initiating input.

SurfaceDialog.description: surface.dialog data, private to the subscribed owning connection. Completed once by surface.answer, safely dismissed when the connection or stream closes.

dialog.description: Required for dialogClosed. The invalidated dialog id on this stream. The viewer dismisses its picker without sending an answer or file bytes.

SurfaceNotice.description: surface.notice data, private to the subscribed owning connection. Downloads remain drawing-machine files. Folder uploads and file inputs in frames remain refused.

SurfaceEvent.description: Private pushed events, never board broadcasts. Canonical board id and matching subscription are required on the owning connection.

BoardLifecycleEvent.description: Board availability after a successful registry transition. The envelope names the canonical board and data is empty. Closing does not disconnect subscriptions; reopening the board announces its availability on those same subscriptions.

MessageId.description: A message's id: `msg_` and 8 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`; easl's own (`msg_` and a ULID) or the one its sender gave (agent.prompt `message`)

AnchorState.description: live: the anchored lines are where written; relocated: found elsewhere by content, or longer or shorter by lines inserted or removed inside; stale: the content is gone (a note shows its last text dimmed, a code tile an untinted range); applied: a proposal whose text the file already reads; missing: no such file or commit

range.description: where it resolved (absent when stale or missing)

AnchorStatus.description: how an anchored range (a note fence, a code tile's range) resolves against disk now

Zoom.description: how big the tile's content draws inside its frame, in place (1.5 is 150%): the frame never changes with it and the title bar stays at 1×; the body lays out at body ÷ zoom and draws zoom× (terminal: bigger text, fewer columns and rows, the program gets the new grid; browser, html: like page zoom, the viewport is body ÷ zoom; code, note, changes: text bigger and rewrapped; diagram: bigger). An object.update that sets it never changes the frame: resize the tile for more room. Out-of-range values clamp; 1 is written as absent. Not on image tiles (the picture is already fitted to the frame; make the tile bigger). The user sets it with the title bar's − % + (the % resets to 100%) or Object › Content Zoom (Zoom Content In ⌃⌘=, Out ⌃⌘-, the presets, Reset Content Zoom ⌃⌘0). Replaces `scale`, which object.create/update/upsert/batch and object.measure reject with invalid_params

error.description: with `idle`: the agent's last turn ended on this error instead of finishing (agent.report `error`), and no turn has started since; `message` says it too unless that report gave its own. It stays through reports that start no turn (`idle` without an error, `unknown`) and through agent.restart, so a relaunched agent's first `idle` doesn't hide it; the next turn (`working`) clears it, and the user seeing the tile doesn't. Absent for a turn that finished

restored.description: a `working` or `blocked` the app restored from before it last closed, which the agent hasn't confirmed since (no report, live or spooled, yet): what it was, maybe not what it is now. `agent.prompt` refuses a restored `working` (read the screen first) unless `force`

via.description: an agent without a lifecycle integration: its terminal notifications (OSC 9/777, a bell) set `done` (`idle` while the user looks), Return typed into it or `agent.prompt` sets `unknown` until the next one; never `working` or `blocked`

ObjectKey.description: any object: a name a script finds it by (`object.find`, `object.upsert`), e.g. a ticket id on the group that is its region. Unique on its board: taking one another object holds is `conflict`, naming the holder; null removes it

command.description: argv run inside the zmx session

host.description: an ssh target (`deckbox`): the terminal's session runs on that machine under its easld (`session.spawn`), and the tile attaches to it over ssh with this app's socket forwarded back, so the agent's integration and the `easl` CLI there reach this board (docs/contracts.md "Hosted terminals"). `cwd` is a directory on that machine. Absent: this Mac. Fixed at creation: an update that changes or removes it is `invalid_params`

name.description: a name other agents address this terminal by: `name` or `name@board` as agent.prompt/wait/read `target` (docs/contracts.md, Agent addresses). Unique within its board is enough; renaming keeps the old name as an alias until another terminal on the board takes it

agent.description: the agent reporting in this tile. When the tile's session is gone (a reboot) it resumes `sessionId` (`omp --resume`, `claude --resume`, `codex resume`); agent.restart relaunches it with `model` and `thinking`. Removed when the agent exits (agent.release)

protocol.description: the integration protocol version it reports (agent.report `protocol`)

model.description: the model it runs, as its integration last reported it (agent.report_session `model`, omp: `provider/id`)

thinking.description: its thinking level, as its integration last reported it (agent.report_session `thinking`, omp: `off` … `max`)

draft.description: its input editor holds text the user hasn't sent (agent.report `draft`); absent: its integration doesn't say

pid.description: the agent's process id, as its integration last reported it (agent.report `pid`)

follow.description: follow mode: false after the user closes the terminal's follow tile (or turns Follow Files off); follow.report is then ignored until it is true again

worktree.description: written by easl: the top level of the worktree of the board's repository the terminal was created in (its `cwd`'s); what it started in, not updated when the shell moves

branch.description: written by easl with `worktree`: the branch checked out there when the terminal was created; absent on a detached HEAD

id.description: the drawing Mac's persistent client.attach identity, independent of its connection id and hostname

host.description: the machine's display name, retained for offline notices; never used for routing

urlIntent.description: Host-owned easld navigation intent, distinct from the observed url. An explicit string URL update stamps the assigned URL, resulting object rev and actor credited with that assignment; URL removal or non-string replacement clears it. Undo or rollback restoration of an existing browser whose URL or intent changed stamps the restored observed URL, new object rev and restored snapshot's updatedBy or createdBy actor, or clears the marker when the restored URL is absent or non-string. Browser reports and unrelated edits or restorations preserve the complete marker, including its original actor. Caller-supplied markers are discarded on creation/import and ignored on update. Mac-hosted boards do not consume this marker

title.description: names the tile; the app never overwrites it

pageTitle.description: written by the app: the page's own title; shown when `title` is unset; never bumps rev

drawingMachine.description: the Mac that runs this page in its own browser profile. Mac-hosted boards run on their host and reject foreign or cleared assignments until machine switching is supported; imported browsers bind to the host. Easld persists the creating Mac's identity, or the first eligible attached Mac for an existing unassigned tile. Disconnect never moves a page to another machine

profile.description: a named browser profile: its own cookies, logins and storage, shared by every tile that names it; absent: the default profile. Tiles a page opens (links, popups) take it

reloadOnChange.description: a page served from this Mac (localhost, 127.x, [::1], a .localhost name, a file) reloads when a file under the board root (a file page: its folder) changes; hidden files and folders and node_modules don't count

path.description: path relative to the board root (relative to your own checkout when you work in another worktree of the board's repository: stored absolute there), or absolute

range.description: lines to scroll to and tint; the tile always shows the whole file. Kept on the code it showed: when lines are inserted or removed above or inside it, the tile re-finds it by content and writes the moved range back (no rev, no undo step); code that is gone leaves it untinted with a stale warning in the header (not follow tiles or pinned tiles)

anchor.description: the range's first line (trimmed), which re-finds the range after lines move; written back by the tile, or given with the range. An update that changes range or path without an anchor drops it

symbol.description: the declaration the range shows; with a range it only names it, and `size: "fit"` fits the range

caption.description: one-line subtitle under the tile's header (plain text, `inline code` allowed); never wraps: object.measure and size "fit" widen the tile to show all of it, and layout.check reports a caption its frame cuts off (`truncated`)

diffBase.description: gutter signs show changes against this: merge-base | head | <sha>

followOf.description: terminal tile this follow tile tracks

lastAction.description: follow tiles: what the agent last did at this location

lastChanges.description: follow tiles: the hunks the agent's last edit here changed (`follow.report` `changes`), which the tile flashes

history.description: follow tiles: recent locations, newest first, without repeats; a location once edited or written keeps that action when read again, and past 8 entries the oldest reads go first, so every edit of a burst stays listed

ref.description: a branch (or any ref) the tile is anchored to instead of one checkout; `path` is relative to the board root's place in the repository (an absolute path in any worktree of the repository means the same repo path). While a worktree of the repository has the ref checked out the tile reads that working tree live: gutter against `diffBase` (default its merge-base), edits reload (header: "live in <worktree>"). Otherwise it reads git objects at the ref, read-only like `pinnedCommit` ("<ref> @ <sha>"). Once the ref no longer resolves (worktree and branch deleted) it reads `refSha`: when the default branch contains it, at the commit that merged it ("merged in <sha>"), else at `refSha` itself ("branch gone, showing <sha>") while its objects exist. `pinnedCommit`, when also set, wins and the ref is ignored. A ref that resolves to nothing (and no `refSha` whose objects remain) is `not_found` on create or update

refSha.description: written by easl: the full SHA `ref` last resolved to (the live worktree's HEAD, or the ref's commit), recorded on every resolve without a rev or undo step, so the tile keeps reading once its worktree and branch are deleted. May be given with `ref` (e.g. by a script that knows the tip)

pinnedCommit.description: a commit (sha, tag, branch, e.g. `HEAD~3` or a fetched `pull/12/head`'s sha): the tile shows the file as of that commit, read-only, with no diff gutter or base picker (header: "pinned at <sha>"); measure, fit, layout.check, line anchors, and renders use that text. The working tree plays no part. Unknown commit or file: the tile says so, and a create or update that needs its text (`size: fit`, a symbol) fails with `not_found`. A path in another worktree of the repository (absolute) is read in that worktree

markdown.description: Markdown. Code fence info strings pick a mode: ```ts file=path#L10-40``` (or symbol=Name, optionally with file=) is a live excerpt of the file; add `propose` to render the fence body as a diff against that range; file=path@<sha>#L10-40 pins to a commit; anchor="first line text" re-finds the range when lines move. Any other fence is free-written. path:line references are clickable wherever they appear: prose, headings, table cells, inline code, free-written fences.

title.description: shown in the tile's title bar (default "Note") and Go to

ref.description: a branch (or any ref) whose tree the note's paths resolve in, instead of `root` (which it overrides): the worktree that has it checked out, live, else git objects at the ref, falling back like CodeProps.ref once it is merged or deleted (via `refSha`). Excerpt fences without their own `@<sha>` read there; path:line links open code tiles with the same `ref`. The markdown stays inline, and images still load from the board's checkout when no worktree has the ref

refSha.description: written by easl: the SHA `ref` last resolved to (as CodeProps.refSha)

root.description: the directory the note's relative paths resolve against (path:line and markdown links, excerpt fences, images): the board's checkout or another worktree of its repository, absolute or board-relative (e.g. ../wt-agent). Default: the board root; a note an agent creates from another worktree than the board's gets that worktree (the same place in it as the board root). Anything else is invalid_params

html.description: page body (or a full document); the kit (Tailwind, Mermaid, canvas-code/link/decisions/compare) is preloaded

ref.description: a branch (or any ref) whose tree canvas-code excerpts and canvas-link resolve in, instead of `root`: as NoteProps.ref. The page body stays inline; img and other page files load from the live worktree, else the board's checkout

refSha.description: written by easl: the SHA `ref` last resolved to (as CodeProps.refSha)

root.description: the directory the page's relative paths resolve against (canvas-link, canvas-code, img): as NoteProps.root

items.description: host, host:port, or *.host; http/https/ws to anything else is blocked

state.description: tile state written by the page through its channel (e.g. canvas-decisions choices by key); at most 256 KiB

root.description: another worktree of the board's repository to review (absolute or board-relative, e.g. ../wt-agent; default: the board root, or your own checkout when you work in another worktree of the board's repository). Anything that isn't a worktree of the board's repository lists nothing and says so. Its files have absolute paths

base.description: what the changes are against: HEAD (the uncommitted work, staged or not: what an agent just did) | merge-base (with the default branch: everything the branch changed, a PR's view) | a commit or ref. The user picks it in the tile's header too. Against anything but HEAD, committed hunks can't be discarded. With `head` or `ref` it defaults to merge-base, and the diff is against the merge-base of `head` with it (`git diff base...head`, a PR's view)

head.description: compare two commits instead of a worktree: any commit or ref (a branch, origin/x, a fetched pull/N/head) against its merge-base with `base` (e.g. {"base": "origin/main", "head": "fm/rel-12389"}). Read from git objects, no checkout; renames and deletions included; read-only: no Stage, Unstage, or Discard. Clicking a line opens a code tile pinned to that side's commit. A ref the repository lacks lists nothing and names the exact `git fetch` that brings it: easl never fetches

ref.description: a branch, instead of `root`: while a worktree of the board's repository has it checked out, that worktree (live, as `root`); otherwise its commits against `base` from git objects, read-only (as `head`). Once the branch is gone it reads `refSha`, and says `merged in <sha>` or `branch gone`. object.create/update resolve it and record `refSha`; a ref that resolves to nothing is not_found, naming the `git fetch` that brings it

refSha.description: written by the tile: the commit `ref` named when the tile last read it, what it falls back to once the branch is deleted

paths.description: files or directories to limit it to, relative to `root` (default the board root) or absolute (default: all of it); a path outside that worktree lists nothing and says so

reviewed.description: written by the tile: the Stage, Unstage, and Discard actions the user took, oldest first (⌘Z of one removes its entry). Agents read it; writing it changes nothing in git

action.description: revert: the user's Discard; unstage: taken out of the index

scope.description: lines: some lines of one hunk the user selected

hunk.description: the hunk's stable id as `object.get` gave it (scope hunk or lines)

header.description: the hunk's `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` at the time (scope hunk or lines)

label.description: how the tile named the hunk: `Lines 15–46`

patch.description: the unified patch applied (at most 200 lines): staged as is to the index; a discard's is the base → working tree diff (HEAD → working tree against an older base) applied reversed (`applied: reversed`), so its `-` lines are what came back and its `+` lines what went; an unstage's is the HEAD → index diff applied reversed to the index

viewed.description: written by the tile: files the user marked Viewed (path → a fingerprint of their diff then). A file counts as viewed (folded, `changes.files[].viewed`) only while its diff is unchanged

path.description: the image file: board-relative or absolute (png, jpg, gif, webp, heic, tiff, bmp, svg, or a pdf's first page). The tile shows it at its aspect ratio and reloads when the file changes on disk, so re-save a chart to the same path to update it

caption.description: one line under the picture (truncated when longer than the tile is wide)

title.description: shown in the title bar and Go to (default: the file name)

path.description: video file on the board's host, board-relative or an allowed absolute path

poster.description: optional poster image on the board's host

DiagramSource.description: Where a graph node came from: the terminal tile, agent session, message or board that holds the observation or argument it states. A click on the node's source badge focuses the terminal a session or tile names when it is on this board; other fields stay a record and the tile says the source isn't on this board

session.description: an agent session id (`props.agent.sessionId`) or session path (`props.agent.sessionPath`) of a terminal on the board

message.description: the message or prompt the claim came from

board.description: the board the tile is on; another board is not resolvable from this one

tile.description: the terminal tile it came from

DiagramProps.description: A diagram tile: `kind: calls` (the default) is a call graph computed from the code by the language server and kept live; `kind: graph` is a knowledge or reasoning graph the caller supplies, which nothing computes. kind calls: a function (the root) and its callers (direction incoming), callees (outgoing) or both, `depth` levels out, as a layered graph of symbol-anchored nodes (name, container, path:line, 1-3 excerpt lines: a caller's calls, else the signature). Only functions in the files of the checkout it is of are nodes: the one its root's file lies in (a worktree's file: that worktree), else yours when you work in another worktree, else the board root's. The graph is computed when the tile is created or re-aimed, again when a file it shows changes on disk, and on `object.reload` (which waits for it); nodes re-resolve by symbol, so code moving keeps them, and a node whose symbol is gone from its file stays with a stale badge (`graph.nodes[].stale`) until it is back or the diagram is aimed elsewhere. Clicking a node with + opens its next level (`expanded`, undoable); its path:line opens the code; a Hyper-click mentions its symbol and lines (a code mention) or the excerpt line under the pointer. An arrow end binds to a node with `{object, node}`.

kind.description: calls: a function and its call hierarchy, computed by the language server. graph: a caller-supplied knowledge or reasoning graph: `knowledge.nodes` (id, label, detail, level, sources, status) and `knowledge.edges` (from premise to conclusion, optional label), laid out one column per reasoning depth; never computed from code, and object.reload is a no-op success

symbol.description: the root function: `Type.member` or a bare name, parameter labels optional (`SocketServer.start`, `AgentReportSpool.read`, `read(from:tiles:)`). Without `path`, the board's files are searched for its declaration

path.description: the file declaring the root, board-relative (relative to your own checkout when you work in another worktree) or absolute

line.description: without `symbol`: the root's declaration line (or a line inside its body) in `path`. Only the first computation reads it: after that the root is re-found by the symbol found there

direction.description: incoming: who calls it (callers left of it); outgoing: what it calls (right of it); both

depth.description: levels shown each side of the root without clicking; nodes on the last level show + when not yet expanded

expanded.description: kind calls only: node ids from graph.nodes[].id opened one level past depth; a click toggles one

title.description: default: `Callers of <symbol>` (`Calls from`, `Calls around`); `Graph` for kind graph

graph.description: Calls-only cache written by the app through bookkeeping, without a rev or undo step. Ignored for kind graph, which reads only knowledge. The next calls computation replaces caller writes

aim.description: the kind, path, symbol, line and direction it was computed for

id.description: path#Container.name, stable while the symbol exists. What expanded and arrow ends name

container.description: calls nodes: the enclosing type or module, when the server says

kind.description: calls nodes: LSP symbol kind: method, function, constructor, …

line.description: calls nodes: 1-based line of its name

excerpt.description: calls nodes: 1-3 lines, a caller's calls toward the root or the signature

stale.description: its symbol is gone from its file: shown as it last was, badged

expandable.description: its next level hasn't been asked for: a click (or adding its id to `expanded`) opens it

lines.description: calls edges: 1-based lines of the calls, in the caller's file

error.description: why the graph is empty or old: no language server for the file, the symbol isn't found, the server failed or has no call hierarchy. The last good graph stays

knowledge.description: Authored data for kind graph. This is the only public input and persisted value for authored graphs; props.graph is an ignored legacy calls cache. Create and update normalize label to name and fill omitted levels with longest-path reasoning depth from premises at 0. A cycle needs an explicit level on every node. Limits count UTF-8 bytes: 500 nodes, 2000 unique directed edges, 256 per id or edge label or source field, 512 per node label, 8192 per detail, and 8 sources per node. Reverse edges are distinct. Reload never computes or writes knowledge.

aim.description: Written on normalization with kind graph and direction incoming

id.description: Non-empty caller id, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes

label.description: Nonblank node label, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes; normalized to name

name.description: Normalized label; accepted when label is absent

level.description: Finite, exactly representable host integer; omitted levels are computed

detail.description: Markdown or plain text, at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes

lines.description: Written as an empty array on normalization

QuestionProps.description: A question an agent (or a script elsewhere) asks the user on the board instead of in chat; the user answers it on its tile (`easl ask` is the CLI for it). Lifecycle: status open → answered | cancelled | expired, each final; a closed question takes only `archived`, `keep`, and `archiveAfter` (and key, zoom). Validated on create and update (invalid_params names the rule): option ids unique, `correct`, `recommended` and `answer.option` name an option, `answer.confidence` only on a question asked with `askConfidence`, `answer` exactly when answered. A new question without a frame is sized from its props: 460 wide, 194 + 50 per option (+ 30 with context, + 30 with askConfidence) tall while open; closing it shrinks it to 148 (+ 40 with a note). Open questions are on the user's ⌘J needs-you list and the board's open-asks count. Answered, it reaches the asker as an object.updated event and, when `asker.tile` is a terminal on the board, as a mention of the question with that terminal's next prompt (never typed into it). An open question past `expiresAt` becomes expired (by easl, no undo step). A closed question that is not kept is archived by the host `archiveAfter` seconds after its `updatedAt` (default 10, at most 86400), on the same timer as expiry, as the app's own write (object.updated, persisted, no undo step). `keep: true` exempts that, not expiry or an explicit archive. null removes `keep` or `archiveAfter` and restores the default. Moving, zooming, changing retention, or unarchiving restarts the delay from the new `updatedAt`.

options.description: what the user picks from (number keys 1–9 pick on the tile); may be empty, then the answer is a note

id.description: unique among the options; what `answer.option` names

why.description: the case for it, shown under the label

recommended.description: the id of the option the asker recommends; the tile marks it

correct.description: the id of the option that is right: easl stamps `answer.correct` (true for it, false for another) when the question is answered, and the closed tile marks it and shows its why. The tile never marks it while the question is open

askConfidence.description: true adds a confidence slider to the open tile: the user sets 0–100% before answering (optional: skipping it leaves `answer.confidence` out), and the answer line the asker gets says how sure the user was

context.description: what to look at before answering; each a link on the tile that opens beside it

asker.description: who asks: a terminal on the board (`tile`; the answer is handed to it), or a name (an agent elsewhere, a script) on an optional host; at least one of tile and name. Default: the calling terminal (`caller`); a create without either is invalid_params

status.description: written open on create; answered with `answer` (the user's pick on the tile, or an object.update), cancelled (the asker took it back: `easl ask cancel`, or the user dismissed it), expired (by easl at `expiresAt`)

expiresAt.description: when an open question stops waiting (RFC 3339); none by default

answer.description: with status answered only: the picked option and/or a note (at least one); `at`, `by` and, on a question with `correct`, `correct` are written by easl when the question becomes answered

confidence.description: how sure the user was, 0–1, on a question asked with `askConfidence`; absent when they answered without setting the slider. Callers may answer with it; without `askConfidence` it is invalid_params

correct.description: written by easl on a question with `correct`: true when the picked option is it, false when another is. Absent on a note-only answer; a caller may send only the value easl would stamp

by.description: who answered: the user, or an agent's terminal (`caller`)

archived.description: true hides a closed question's tile (archive is not a status: `status` keeps how it ended, `answer` stays); an open question can't be archived. The host also sets it when a closed question's archive delay elapses

keep.description: true exempts a closed question from automatic archiving; it does not stop expiry or an explicit archive. Absent or false is not exempt. May change after closure; null removes it

archiveAfter.description: seconds after updatedAt before a closed, unkept question is archived. The implicit delay is 10 for stored questions without a readable value. On create, an absent or null value uses the host's questionArchiveAfter app setting or easld --question-archive-after default; a nondefault host delay is stored in this prop. An explicit value wins. A fraction is a fraction of a second. May change after closure; null then restores the implicit 10

points.description: ink points [x, y, pressure?] in object-local coordinates

color.description: palette name (black, grey, blue, green, orange, red, violet) or #rrggbb

fill.description: rect/ellipse interior; only filled interiors hit-test, so an unfilled shape never blocks what is beneath it

textSize.description: text shapes only: a multiplier of the 20-pt text font; the frame grows with it (a corner drag on a text shape scales text and box together, as does Object › Content Zoom). Rect and ellipse labels don't take it; ignored on other kinds

lines.description: on a code tile, the end attaches to the tile's left or right edge at the row of `lines.start` as the tile shows it (scrolled to its range: up to 3 rows of context above it); a line scrolled out of view attaches at the top of the code or the bottom of the tile. Other tiles: the whole tile

node.description: on a diagram tile, a node id (knowledge.nodes[].id for kind graph, graph.nodes[].id for kind calls): the end attaches to that node's box as the tile draws it, and follows it when the graph changes. Other tiles: the whole tile

relation.description: semantic edge type, e.g. hypothesis_about, calls, depends_on

label.description: caption drawn beside the route. Absent: the arrow shows its `relation` (secondary color) instead; "" shows no caption

route.description: straight: one segment between the facing sides; orthogonal: horizontal/vertical segments with one jog; avoid: horizontal/vertical segments around every tile (and text or filled shape) in the way, routed together with the board's other avoid arrows: arrows sharing a side get their own ports, arrows sharing a channel run in parallel tracks, and they follow their group's `flow`. Arrows between the same two objects (either direction) are drawn apart automatically; labels sit beside their own route, clear of boxes, group titles, other arrows and other labels where possible (else a short leader away).

GroupProps.description: A group is a region: its frame is always its members' bounds plus `padding`, with a 32 pt title band on top, kept current as members move, resize, or go away (a `frame` passed for a group is ignored). `object.get --as graph` encloses what lies inside that frame.

title.description: shown in the title band; the band is the group's drag handle

color.description: palette name or #rrggbb, as ShapeProps.color; tints the region and title

padding.description: space between the members' bounds and the region's edge

flow.description: which way the diagram inside reads: `avoid` arrows among the members leave the side of their source facing downstream and enter their target's upstream side where they can. Absent: inferred from the way arrows between groups point

w.description: wrap width for notes and text; for code the widest the tile may get (default 1546, 200 columns), past which long lines wrap; for html the width the page lays out at (default 640)

FitFrame.description: with size: fit (or for a new note), where the object goes; the rest of its frame is measured

SizeFrame.description: just a size: the object gets it and is placed as without a frame (the free spot nearest the calling agent's terminal)

FramePatch.description: any of x, y, w, h; the rest keep their current values (with size: fit, w is the wrap or widest width and h is measured)

frame.description: the whole box the object draws; an arrow's is the bounds of its routed line as drawn (bound ends follow what they point at)

expires.description: absolute RFC3339 deletion deadline, set by the host; absent when no expiry is scheduled

props.description: one of TerminalProps | BrowserProps | CodeProps | NoteProps | HtmlProps | ChangesProps | ImageProps | VideoProps | DiagramProps | QuestionProps | ShapeProps | ArrowProps | GroupProps, selected by type (`easl methods CodeProps` lists one)

updatedAt.description: seconds since 2001-01-01T00:00:00Z, matching the object's API updatedAt

reasons.description: all applicable reasons, in the listed order

kind.description: a console message; an uncaught error or unhandled promise rejection; a request that failed (HTTP status 400 or more, a network error, a resource that didn't load)

text.description: the message as the console prints it (up to 1,000 characters), or `METHOD url → status`

source.description: `url:line:column` of the code that logged (warnings and errors) or threw

status.description: a failed request's HTTP status; absent when it got none (network error, a resource load WebKit reports without one)

resource.description: what made the request: fetch, xhr, document (the page itself), or the element (img, script, link…)

PageLog.description: What a browser tile's page reported since it loaded. Main frame only; a new document (load, reload) starts over.

loaded.description: false: the tile has no page now (never shown or rendered, or released while out of view); `view.render` loads it

visibility.description: how WebKit runs the page now: visible (on screen, rAF at the display's rate), hidden (nobody sees it: no rAF, timers throttled more the longer it stays hidden), driven (kept running for an agent though nobody sees it: rAF irregular and slower), released (no page)

previous.description: the log of the page easl last released (after `since` when it names that page), as it was then; returned until the page loads another document after the reload, and until `since` names the current document

errors.description: exceptions, console errors and failed requests since the page loaded

entries.description: oldest first, the latest 100 (after `since`); the page keeps its last 200 errors and warnings and last 200 other messages

omitted.description: older entries after `since` left out of `entries`

dropped.description: entries the page's buffers no longer hold

reloaded.description: `since` named an earlier document: `entries` start at this one's beginning

cursor.description: pass as `since` to read only what comes after; while released, the released page's (`previous.cursor`)

vitals.description: milliseconds from navigation start (CLS unitless); null when not measured yet or not measured by WebKit (then named in `unsupported`), never a stand-in zero

side.description: diff side of the lines; absent outside a diff

commit.description: with side old or absent: the commit whose version of path holds the lines (deleted diff rows, pinned excerpts); with side new: the diff base. Absent: the working tree

diff.description: a changes tile's line or hunk: what the lines are in the diff and the hunk's index state, e.g. `added line · unstaged hunk`, `removed line · partly staged hunk`, `whole hunk +3 −1 · staged`

point.description: a Hyper-click on a ,

part.description: what `text` is: the user's selection; the screen rows around a Hyper-click, the clicked row marked `> ` and the others indented two spaces; or one command's output (Hyper-click inside it, with Ghostty's shell integration)

command.description: with part command: what ran (exit and duration only for the shell's last command)

x.description: the point on the image, in the image's own pixels from its left edge

oneOf.description: what a browser tile's page reported (a Hyper-click in the tile's error list): a console message, an uncaught error, or a failed request

a block of a note (a Hyper-click in its body): the paragraph, list item with its nested items, quote, table row, fence, or heading with its section, as it read when staged; the drain re-finds it by its text in the note as it is then

headings.description: the headings of the sections it sits in, outermost first

lines.description: its lines in the note's markdown when staged

text.description: its markdown when staged (indentation removed), at most 40 lines and 2000 characters

stagedAt.description: Staging time: API seconds since 2001-01-01 or an RFC 3339 timestamp.

summary.description: compact text for prompt context: location, excerpt, relations

graph.description: structured view: contents, encloses, overlaps, arrows

object.description: an object on the target terminal's board

lines.description: code tiles only: these lines of its file (at its pinned commit, if any). Without it a code tile showing a range mentions that range

point.description: image tiles only: a pixel of the picture, in the image's own pixels from its top-left

PromptMention.description: A board object `agent.prompt` attaches for the receiving agent, as a Hyper-click would mention it: a code tile's lines, an image tile's pixel, else the whole object

board.description: the board the terminal is on

address.description: how to reach this terminal as a `target` from any board, resolving to it alone: `name@board` (the board's name is its root folder's name) for a named terminal, `name@<board id>` while another open board's folder has that name too (or its own is gone), its tile id when it has no name or another terminal on its board has the same one

aliases.description: names it had before a rename that still reach it on its board (until another terminal there takes them); absent when none

protocol.description: the integration protocol version its agent's integration last reported (agent.report `protocol`); 1 and later take out-of-band messages (agent.inbox). Absent: none reported, or the integration died without releasing the terminal (killed: its shell came back to the prompt)

kind.description: the integrated agent that reported (omp, claude, codex, gemini, opencode), or the program of an agent reporting by notification (aider; lifecycle `via: "notifications"`), else unknown

title.description: the title the program in the terminal set (OSC 0/2), e.g. Gemini CLI's "✋ Action Required (glow)"; absent when none

program.description: what runs in the terminal's foreground, named the way a person would (`gemini`, `opencode`, `cargo test`); absent at the shell's prompt

lastCommand.description: the last command the terminal's shell finished (Ghostty's shell integration reports it); absent until one did

open.description: its board is open in easl. false: a tile of a closed board, as its saved board file has it (lifecycle `state`, `seen`, `restored` as last saved; no title, program or last command)

live.description: its zmx session runs (a session labelled `canvas.board=<board> canvas.tile=<tile>` by this easl instance; docs/contracts.md); a hosted terminal's (`props.host`) as its host's easld lists it (`session.list`). Absent when easl can't tell (no zmx; a host it isn't connected to, or that doesn't answer)

pid.description: the agent's process on this machine: the pid its integration reported (agent.report `pid`) while that process lives, else the foreground process of the tile's zmx session; absent when nothing but its shell runs there, the session is gone, or it runs on another machine (a hosted terminal)

focused.description: the terminal has keyboard focus in the key window while easl is the frontmost app: the user may be typing in it. Always false on a closed board

draft.description: its agent's input editor holds unsent text (agent.report `draft`, omp's extension); absent when its integration doesn't say

model.description: the model its agent runs, as its integration last reported it (agent.report_session `model`)

thinking.description: its agent's thinking level, as its integration last reported it (agent.report_session `thinking`)

id.description: `msg_…`; ack it (agent.inbox `ack`) once the agent has it

attribution.description: agent: a terminal sent it (`caller`); user: a script with no tile (its `from` label), on the user's behalf

when.description: now: into the running turn (a steer) or a new turn when idle; next-turn: never into a running turn, only once it has ended

mentions.description: the board objects the sender attached (agent.prompt `mentions`); absent when none

context.description: those mentions resolved now, as the hand-off block a drain gives (`<canvas-mentions …>` naming the sender); absent when none

AgentMessage.description: An out-of-band message queued for a terminal whose integration takes messages (agent.report `protocol` ≥ 1)

tile.description: the sending terminal; absent for a script

name.description: the sending terminal's name as the tray shows it now (its `name`, else its title, else `Terminal`), or the script's `from` label (default `script`)

address.description: where a reply goes: the sending terminal's address (as Agent's: `name@board`, `name@<board id>` or its tile id); absent for a script (nothing to reply to)

MessageSender.description: Who sent a message, resolved when it is taken (agent.inbox): a renamed sender shows its new name

command.description: the command line (its first line), as the shell integration titled the terminal while it ran; for an older block, the prompt row above its output

exit.description: exit status; null when the shell didn't report one

root.description: the board's root: a repository board's is its main checkout, whichever worktree opened it; otherwise the directory the board was last opened at

archived.description: the root directory no longer exists (e.g. a removed checkout); the board is kept

open.description: the board has a window in the app (only open boards accept `board` params)

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 time the board was last saved; absent for a board never saved

repo.description: a repository board's common git directory (its identity: one board per repository)

worktrees.description: a repository board's worktrees: its repository's live ones (main checkout first) and every one the board has seen (opened from, a terminal started in, a merged per-branch board's), one entry per worktree and branch

RemoteBoardInfo.description: An open remote tab in the Mac app's board.list. The host owns its board id and root. Local-only metadata is absent.

host.description: the host as the tab names it

board.description: the board's id on the host, not a local mirror id

root.description: the board's root on the host, not a local filesystem path

title.description: the tab's title, as board.open_remote returns it

window.description: the tab's window number, as board.open_remote returns it

branch.description: the branch checked out there (live), or last seen there; absent on a detached HEAD

live.description: the worktree exists with this branch checked out

main.description: the repository's main checkout (the board root)

region.description: the group holding what this branch's board held before boards were per repository (props.key `branch:<name>`)

Viewport.description: What the board's window shows: `rect` is the visible board area in board coordinates, `zoom` the magnification (1 = 100%, one point per board unit).

RenderedObject.description: Where an object landed in a rendered image and whether its content really painted.

pixelRect.description: image pixels, top-left origin; a tile's rect is its frame (its 26 pt title bar is inside it)

state.description: placeholder: content not loaded in time or not renderable (a stand-in was drawn); failed: rendering errored

reason.description: why a tile is a placeholder or failed

contentSize.description: the content's own extent in board points at the tile's width, below its title bar (tiles only; a zoomed tile's layout extent times its `zoom`); code: its range's rows and longest line under the header, the whole file without a range (what size "fit" shows)

overflow.description: board points of content beyond the frame (right, bottom); absent when it fits

seq.description: log cursor; pass the largest seen as `since`

rev.description: board revision right after the entry (viewport/selection entries don't change it)

actor.description: `user`, `system`, or `agent:<terminal tile id>`; a cascade is credited to whoever made the change that caused it

id.description: the object (for follow: the follow tile)

cause.description: set on cascades of another change, saying why: a group `fit to its members` (one entry per group per revision, at its net change), an arrow's end freed because its `bound object obj_… deleted`

MetricsTally.description: one window of a counter: how many, how long (ms, and the longest) and how many bytes; ms and bytes only when the counter has them

MetricsCounter.description: a counter since launch (or the last reset), over the last 60 s, and over the last 10 min

image.preview.description: Read an image object's file under HostFiles.boardImage authorization and its 4194304-byte limit. Return original for unsupported formats, animated PNG (acTL before IDAT), EXIF orientation other than 1, natural long edge no larger than maxPixels, more than 16000000 natural pixels, or PNG output no smaller than the source. Invalid PNG/JPEG raster data is unreadable. Preview preserves alpha and aspect ratio without upscaling: long edge maxPixels, short edge max(1, round(naturalShort * maxPixels / naturalLong)). Version uses the stable read descriptor's exact nanosecond metadata. File errors are refused, not_found, too_large, unreadable or unavailable; request/type errors are invalid_params. Original explicitly selects original-file transport, not an error fallback.

surface.stream.description: Open a connection-owned stream of the existing browser WKWebView, not a new page. Requires events.subscribe for surface.frame and the tile's canonical board on this same connection. Starts with outstanding frame 0. No frame event precedes surface.ack frame 0. At most one logical frame is outstanding and credits never accumulate. Acknowledge only after complete decoding and presentation. JPEG is the default. Explicit PNG remains lossless. Explicit h264 negotiates adaptive JPEG or predicted ESV1 motion with a bounded sharp H264 reference. Refresh uses ordered 16 KiB chunks with one outstanding chunk, and surface.progress never grants decode credit. Input may supersede only refresh. The next frame declares its canceled range and independently resets prediction. New video sessions, resizes, and motion resumption after sharp prediction require a keyframe. Reopen after an undeclared sequence gap or decoding failure. Easld pins the stream to the exact drawingMachine attachment and forwards image bytes unchanged to the owning viewer. Private-event hearing is captured at open. Reopen to use subscriptions added later. Drawing changes, board or tile closure, and either endpoint disconnect end the relay without replay.

surface.ack.description: On the opening connection, acknowledge exactly the outstanding frame to grant one next frame. Initial ack is frame 0. Older acknowledgements are ignored; future frames are invalid_params. Decode and install the image before acknowledging.

surface.progress.description: On the opening connection, receipt one validated refresh chunk by its starting byte offset. The source sends the next 16 KiB chunk only after this receipt, with at most one chunk outstanding. This grants neither frame nor decode credit. Duplicate receipts do nothing. Unsent or misaligned offsets are invalid_params. Superseded refresh receipts do nothing. surface.ack follows assembly, decode, and presentation of the complete logical frame.

surface.input.description: Queue ordered native input for the opening connection's existing browser. Validate the entire bounded batch before any mutation. seq values are positive and strictly increasing within the batch; previously accepted events are ignored. Never automatically resend input. Acceptance means queueing only. If page relay setup fails during delivery, the stream closes with a notice; accepted input is never replayed. A later frame input watermark has the processing limitations documented by SurfaceFrame. Result text is present only for an explicit copy operation.

accepted.description: Count of newly queued events in this batch; duplicates contribute zero. Not a delivery or presentation acknowledgement.

surface.answer.description: Complete one pending dialog on its stream's opening connection. A closed stream safely dismisses pending dialogs. Auth passwords and file bytes are transient request data, never logged, staged or read from the viewer's keychain. A file picker accepts 1 file, or up to 32 with multiple:true, totaling at most 8 MiB decoded. An accepted file selection cannot be empty. Files are installed in the initiating main-frame input as in-memory File objects with untrusted input/change events. Cancellation preserves the input's prior files. Navigation or element replacement invalidates the picker. Cancel carries accept:false and no files.

surface.stop.description: Stop the opening connection's stream and cancel its capture work. Never delete or release the host page; its existing driven-lease policy takes over. Another connection cannot control this stream.

agent.prompt_epoch.description: Discover safe prompt submission support and the current receipt registry incarnation before sending. The epoch changes whenever the host restarts; an older host refuses this method before a composer submits anything.

app.metrics.description: What easl's own work costs, for finding what makes it slow: main-thread busy time and stretches (with the longest one's cause), per-method API requests (`api.<method>`: requests answered, time from arrival to the queued reply, waiting behind earlier requests on the connection included, and reply bytes; `api.in.<method>` requests arrived and their bytes; `api.main.<method>` the main-thread part of its dispatches), events sent, board writes and group refits (top writers), arrow routings (`route.board` the whole board, `route.arrow` one arrow following its ends; top triggering objects), saves, live tiles per kind, HTML page loads, reuses, measures and renders, and the process's CPU, wakeups, memory and energy with its WebKit helpers'. Counters cover three windows: since launch or the last reset, the last 60 s, the last 10 min. `easl metrics [--watch] [--reset]` prints them as text.

reset.description: after reading, clear every counter and the longest stretch (levels such as live tiles stay)

watch.description: sample the process every second for the next 3 s instead of every 10 (a client polling each second)

sinceS.description: seconds since launch or the last reset: the `total` window

gauges.description: current levels: `live.<Tile>` (tiles showing live content, by kind), `html.webviews`, `events.subscribers`

top.description: top offenders since the reset: `writers` (`agent:<tile>` or `user`), `routingTriggers` (the object whose change routed the board; ms the routings took)

longest.description: the longest main-thread stretch since the reset

cause.description: the work it did, longest first, e.g. `api.main.object.update obj_… 1790 ms (route.board 84 arrows 1500 ms)`

stalls.description: main-thread stalls (a turn of a second or more) the app `sample`d itself through, into `stalls/` in its home (the Mac app only; easld has no main thread)

newest.description: home-relative, e.g. `stalls/2026-10-08T051210Z.txt`; also named at the start of that stretch's cause

windows.description: `total`, `last60s`, `last10m`, each with cpuPercent, interruptWakeupsPerS, idleWakeupsPerS, energyMJPerS

helpers.description: WebKit processes easl is responsible for

app.update.description: Check for or install an update of the running Mac app without confirmation UI. App socket only, not forwarded by easld. Install ignores idle, uses the manual update trust checks and returns before the app quits and relaunches in the background with its open boards restored. Failures leave the running app intact and are reported in error.

mode.description: check fetches the latest release; install checks, downloads, verifies and installs a newer release now.

availableVersion.description: The latest feed version, including one that is not newer; null when unknown.

installPending.description: An update is downloading, verifying, waiting in verified staging, or installing.

error.description: The update failure reason, including a retained failure from the previous install; null without a failure.

deferred.description: remote viewer active when automatic installation is deferred for recent remote activity, otherwise null; explicit install still proceeds.

interruptions.description: Live remote sessions that installing now can interrupt.

warning.description: Human-readable interruption warning for explicit installation, otherwise null.

board.get.description: Board manifest: all objects plus a change cursor. Heavy props are summarized (use object.get for them whole): HTML `html` and a follow tile's `history` become a short string, note `markdown` past 400 characters is cut. Objects created or changed since `since` are flagged.

board.description: an open local board id or the host board id of an open remote tab. The Mac app forwards remote board.get to its host. Open and stored local ids, including migrated ids, take precedence; a closed local target remains not_found. Several matching remote tabs are ambiguous

viewer.description: Include only this remote window's retained composer outcome receipts; omitted otherwise.

since.description: board revision cursor from a previous call

branch.description: only branch `branch`'s part of a repository board: the regions keyed `branch:<branch>` and what they hold, objects whose `ref` is the branch, terminals that started on it (`branch`), and arrows between those

merged.description: board ids this repository board took in (`repo.merged`), omitted when empty. A terminal session may still carry one of these original board labels; an attaching client accepts it only when its home and tile labels also match. Absent: only this board's current id owns its terminals

closed.description: True when the Mac host closed this board's tab by hand but keeps its agents running. Omitted while its tab is open and by easld. Remote viewers keep the last seen board read-only until board.opened or a later board.get without closed:true.

attention.description: Unseen markers on the returned objects, sorted by id; omitted when none. A reread replaces the viewer's marker snapshot.

composerReceipts.description: Newest retained composer outcomes for the requested viewer, in order; transient, omitted without viewer or when empty. Each board keeps at most 2000 outcomes across viewers.

regions.description: with `branch`: the ids of the branch's regions (groups keyed `branch:<branch>`), `[]` when it has none

board.undo.description: Undo this remote viewer's latest host-accepted step at or before step. Only fields still equal to the values that step wrote are reverted; concurrent edits remain and their objects appear in kept. The host retains up to 200 steps per viewer in memory. Nothing from another viewer or agent enters this viewer's history.

step.description: The latest local step the viewer intends to undo. A retry of an already-undone step does not undo another step.

board.redo.description: Redo the fields this viewer's undo actually changed. Fields edited since that undo remain unchanged and their objects appear in kept. A new host-accepted step from this viewer clears its redo history.

step.description: The undone step to redo. A retry does not apply the step twice.

board.history.description: Activity log: who created, changed, or deleted what (including objects that existed only for seconds), where the user's viewport settled, what they selected, follow-tile re-aims, app starts, and peer messages that bounced (`message`: its receiver's agent ended before taking it, and the sender was a script or takes no messages; the entry's `id` is the receiver). Plain request/response, cheap to poll: pass the returned `cursor` as `since` next time. In memory, newest 2000 entries per board; an app restart starts a new log with a `restart` entry.

since.description: entries after this `seq` cursor, or after this ISO 8601 time

limit.description: newest entries returned when more match

truncated.description: more entries matched than `limit`, or the ring buffer already dropped some after `since`

restarted.description: `since` is newer than this log: the app restarted, so every entry is returned

board.list.description: Every stored local board, open or not, including archived boards whose root directory is gone. The Mac app appends its open remote tabs with remote:true, host, sshTarget, the host's board id and root, title, window and open:true; closing a remote tab removes its row. Local rows are unchanged and have no remote field. Remote rows have no archived, objects, updatedAt, repo or worktrees metadata; root is on the host. easld lists only its own stored boards, unchanged.

board.stale.description: Read-only cleanup candidates, sorted by id. Reasons are creator-gone (agent creator no longer has a terminal on this board), expired (deadline reached), untouched (updatedAt strictly before now minus olderThan), and exited (terminal process confirmed exited). Does not delete objects or change revisions, timestamps, or events.

olderThan.description: finite nonnegative duration in seconds, minutes, hours or days; fractions allowed

board.open.description: Open the board for a directory (creating it if new) as a tab of the frontmost board window, also when that window is minimized (the tab waits there). A directory in a git repository opens the repository's board (one per repository, rooted at its main checkout), tagged with the worktree it is in: the window names it, New Terminal starts there, and the view goes to its region. The user's current tab stays in front unless `select` is true, which also brings a minimized window back. Opening an already-open board only selects it when `select` is true.

root.description: absolute directory path (`~` allowed): a directory in a git repository opens its repository's board; any other directory its own

select.description: bring the board's tab to the front: this switches the user's tab, so only when they asked to see that board. While the board window is on a Space other than the one on screen, macOS switches to that Space (activating easl) and the tab comes forward there; an instance that never activates (`EASL_NO_ACTIVATE`) leaves the tab to come forward when the user goes there. AppKit would otherwise show the tab on the Space the user is working in

worktree.description: the worktree of the board's repository `root` is in

region.description: its branch's region, which the view went to

board.open_remote.description: The Mac app only (easld answers `unsupported`): open a board another Mac's easl hosts, as File › Open Remote… does, as a tab of the frontmost board window (its own window when there is none), viewed live over ssh (docs/contracts.md "Remote boards"). `host` is found as the picker finds it: the host opened before (`remote-hosts.json`) or the tailnet Mac whose ssh target or name it is, else it is an ssh host as typed into the picker; then the picker's host discovery over ssh, which remembers the host in `remote-hosts.json`, and the board is read from the host. That host list is the only file this writes: the board is viewed, never copied (no board file, viewport, composer or `open-boards.json` entry). The user's current tab stays in front and nothing takes focus unless `select` is true. A board already open from that host is answered (`alreadyOpen`) without asking the host again, selected when `select` is true, never opened twice. Fails `unavailable` when the host can't be reached or its easl doesn't answer, `not_found` when the host has no such board open (its `board.list` says which are `open`), `ambiguous` when two hosts have that name, `invalid_params` for a host that isn't one host (spaces, a leading `-`, `user@` or `@host`) or a board that isn't a board id.

host.description: the host as File › Open Remote… names it: a tailnet Mac's name (`twaldin-work`) or ssh target, a host opened before (`remote-hosts.json` `name` or `sshTarget`), an ssh config alias, or `user@host`

board.description: the board's id on the host (`brd_…`, from its `board.list`); never filled from this terminal's board

select.description: bring the board's tab to the front, as `board.open`'s `select` does: this switches the user's tab, so only when they asked to see that board. Without it the tab opens behind the one in front and nothing takes focus

host.description: the host as the tab names it

sshTarget.description: what ssh connects to (a tailnet Mac's DNS name, else the host as given)

root.description: the board's root on the host

window.description: the tab's window number (each tab is a window), as `screencapture -l` and yabai take it

alreadyOpen.description: the tab was open already: nothing was opened

board.close.description: Close an open board without quitting the server. Save its latest state and remove it from the open set and open-boards.json, but keep its stored board file and board.list entry with open:false. By default terminals and their sessions stay running; board.open of the same root restores them. The Mac app refuses its last open board with conflict, including while hidden or minimized. A remote tab closes only this viewer and never changes the host; any explicit endSessions, including false, is invalid_params there. Unknown or already closed boards are not_found. An affected agent.restart is conflict. Persistence or session-ending failure is unavailable and leaves the board open, with any partial session effects reported. No new event is emitted and subscriptions stay connected.

board.description: defaults as board.export: the client's board environment, otherwise the server's default board including its frontmost fallback

endSessions.description: end local terminal sessions and remove their terminal objects, as the sheet's End Sessions does; easld requires --own-terminals or answers unsupported, and keeps hosted terminals it does not own. Forbidden on a remote tab, even false

kept.description: terminals retained with their sessions, sorted by id

name.description: nonempty props.name, otherwise nonempty props.title, otherwise Terminal

ended.description: terminals whose sessions ended and whose objects were removed, sorted by id

name.description: nonempty props.name, otherwise nonempty props.title, otherwise Terminal

board.export.description: Write a pretty-printed JSON snapshot of an open board (objects, frames, props; not the personal selection tray) into the repo. Committing it is left to the caller.

path.description: absolute, or relative to the board root; default .easl/board.json

object.get.description: Read one object. `as: graph` adds structural relations: encloses, enclosedBy, overlaps, arrowsIn/arrowsOut (arrows bound to it), arrows (arrows drawn inside it, with from/to bindings), and from/to for an arrow. A changes tile adds `changes`: its files and hunks as git has them now (what the user kept), each hunk with its unified `lines`, next to `props.reviewed` (what they staged or discarded, with the patches). A terminal adds `lastCommand` once its shell finished one. A browser tile adds `page`: the console messages, uncaught errors and failed requests its page reported since it loaded (recorded from the first line of the page on), its error and warning counts, and web vitals; pass `page.cursor` back as `since` to read only what came after. A note adds `fences`: each anchored fence's state (live, relocated, stale, applied, missing), resolved range and reason, resolved against disk now; a code tile showing a range adds `rangeStatus`, the same for its range. To look at an object, `view.render` it.

since.description: browser tiles: `page.cursor` from an earlier call; `page.entries` then holds only what the page reported after it (everything, with `reloaded: true`, when the page has loaded again since)

lastCommand.description: terminals only: the last command the shell finished, as in `agent.list`

fences.description: notes only: each anchored fence (excerpt or proposal; fences with the same info string are one) resolved against disk now, as the note shows it

items.description: the fence as written, and its AnchorStatus fields

markdownLines.description: 1-based markdown lines of its opening fence lines

path.description: the file, as written or as a symbol search found it

range.description: where it resolved (absent when stale or missing)

rangeStatus.description: code tiles showing a range (not follow tiles or pinned tiles): how the range resolves against disk now (the tile reloads and re-anchors first, so `object` already carries a re-found range)

baseLabel.description: HEAD, merge-base with main, or the commit as written

notice.description: why nothing is listed (not a repository, no commits, a path outside it, a ref it lacks with the `git fetch` that brings it)

omitted.description: changed files past the 300 the tile loads

head.description: two commits compared (`head`, or a `ref` no worktree has checked out): full SHA of the head; `base` is its merge-base with the base

headLabel.description: two commits compared: the head as written

baseTip.description: two commits compared: full SHA of the commit the base names

readOnly.description: two commits compared: nothing to stage, unstage, or discard

refState.description: a `ref` that no longer resolves, read at `refSha`: `merged in <sha>` or `branch gone`

refSha.description: `ref` tiles: the commit the ref named (the live worktree's HEAD, or the ref's commit)

oldPath.description: renamed files: the name in the base

notice.description: why it has no hunks: binary file, too large to show, submodule, mode changed

viewed.description: the user marked it Viewed and its diff hasn't changed since

id.description: stable while the hunk's lines stay the same (line numbers aside); `props.reviewed[].hunk` names it

status.description: unstaged: the working tree differs from the index there; partial: the index holds some of it (staged, then edited again: committing what's staged leaves the rest out); staged: the index has it; committed: HEAD has it (a base older than HEAD)

lines.description: the hunk as unified-diff lines (` `, `-`, `+`, then the text), at most 200

truncated.description: the hunk has more than 200 lines

object.find.description: Find objects by what they are instead of by id: `key` returns the object holding that `props.key` (ObjectKey) as object.get does (`as: graph` too), or `not_found`; `keyPrefix` lists every object whose key starts with it, in key order ("REL-" for every ticket's region), possibly none; `type` lists every object of that type, oldest first, and with `status` only those whose `props.status` is it (`type: question, status: open`: the questions still waiting on the user). One of key, keyPrefix, type. Per board: `board` defaults as for object.create.

keyPrefix.description: list the objects whose keys start with this

type.description: list the objects of this type

status.description: with `type`: only objects whose props.status is this (a question's open, answered, cancelled, expired)

object.description: `key`: the object, with the rest of object.get's result beside it

objects.description: `keyPrefix`, `type`: the objects, summarized as board.get lists them

object.create.description: Create an object. Omit `frame` (or give only its `w` and `h`) to let the board place it in the free spot nearest the calling agent's terminal (or the viewport center for users): clear of every tile and group, inside the user's view when the terminal is on screen and there's room within 600 pt of it (else beside it, even out of view). A code tile without a frame is as wide as its file's longest line needs at its `zoom`, from 640 up to 200 columns (1546 at zoom 1; the working-tree file, up to 1 MiB; a follow tile and one shown from git, `ref` or `pinnedCommit`, stay 640), and 446 tall. `size: fit` sizes the frame to the content (object.measure; notes and text wrap at `frame.w`; code is at most `frame.w` wide, default 1546 (200 columns), and wraps longer lines; html is `frame.w` wide, default 640, and as tall as its page at that width, at most 4000; changes shows every hunk, as wide as its longest line up to `frame.w`, default 960, longer lines wrapped, at most 4000 tall, and a fitted changes tile grows with its diff; image is its picture at one point per pixel, scaled down to at most `frame.w`, default 960, plus the title bar and caption; a diagram is its graph: kind graph reads `props.knowledge`; a calls diagram without `props.graph` is computed first, waiting for the language server up to 60 s as object.reload does, then fitted, and `diagram` says how that went). A note without a frame height is always fitted to its markdown (at `frame.w`, default 280), and an image to its picture, so `frame` may be just x, y, w (or omitted). A note's line-range fences (`file=…#L…`) are stored with the `anchor=` their tile would write back, so the result's `rev` is the one to update with. The caller's tile (EASL_TILE_ID) becomes createdBy. A changes tile the calling agent already made for the same `root`, `base`, and `paths` is reused rather than duplicated: it takes the call's other props, `frame`, and `size`, and the result says `reused: true`.

props.description: the type's props: TerminalProps, BrowserProps, CodeProps, NoteProps, HtmlProps, ChangesProps, ImageProps, VideoProps, DiagramProps, QuestionProps, ShapeProps, ArrowProps, or GroupProps (`easl methods <Name>` lists one). `scale` is invalid_params (a tile's content zoom is `zoom`, a text shape's font `textSize`)

size.description: measure the frame's size from the content; `frame` then only needs x, y (and w to wrap a note, text, or an html page, or to cap a code tile's width)

expires.description: RFC3339 timestamp with timezone, or null to clear; mutually exclusive with expiresIn

expiresIn.description: finite nonnegative duration (s, m, h, d; fractions allowed), resolved once by the host to absolute expires; mutually exclusive with expires

viewer.description: With step, record this remote window's edit for board.undo. Both fields are required together and forbidden inside object.batch.

step.description: The viewer's gesture id; writes with the same id form one undo step.

caller.description: calling tile id; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

reused.description: a changes tile: the caller's existing tile for the same root, base, and paths came back (updated) instead of a new one

warnings.description: present when `props` has keys this type doesn't define (typos like `colour`): each names the key and the type's props. The props are kept anyway

diagram.description: a diagram created with `size: fit` before it had a graph: object.reload's result for its first one (`loaded` false: still computing when the wait ended, the tile left at its default size, and `warnings` says so)

overlaps.description: `size: fit` only, present when the fitted object covers others (by layout.check's overlap rule; in a batch, once the whole batch is laid out): their ids

approximate.description: the frame was measured (`size: fit`, a note's automatic height) from easld's glyph table or a client's fallback HTML layout, rather than exact Mac layout, as object.measure's `approximate`

object.update.description: Patch an object's frame, stacking order z, and/or props (shallow merge). `frame` may give any of x, y, w, h; the rest stay. Pass `rev` for optimistic concurrency (a note's fences are anchored as on create). `size: fit` re-measures the frame from the (patched) content at its current position and width (code: at most `frame.w`, default 1546; image: at most `frame.w`, default 960; never their current width), or at `frame` x, y, w. Without `frame` x or y it doesn't grow over objects it didn't already overlap: it grows up and/or left instead (keeping its bottom or right edge), else moves to the nearest free spot no farther than its longer side, else grows in place (the result's `overlaps` names what it covers). After changing an html tile's `html` or a note's `markdown`, pass `size: "fit"` in the same update to refit its height to the new content.

z.description: stacking order, back to front; objects with larger values draw above objects with smaller values

size.description: measure the frame's size from the content
