props.description: the type's props: TerminalProps, BrowserProps, CodeProps, NoteProps, HtmlProps, ChangesProps, ImageProps, VideoProps, DiagramProps, QuestionProps, ShapeProps, ArrowProps, or GroupProps (`easl methods <Name>` lists one). `scale` is invalid_params (a tile's content zoom is `zoom`, a text shape's font `textSize`)

expires.description: RFC3339 timestamp with timezone, or null to clear; omission preserves the deadline; mutually exclusive with expiresIn

expiresIn.description: finite nonnegative duration (s, m, h, d; fractions allowed), resolved once by the host to absolute expires; mutually exclusive with expires

viewer.description: With step, record this remote window's edit for board.undo. Both fields are required together and forbidden inside object.batch.

step.description: The viewer's gesture id; writes with the same id form one undo step.

warnings.description: present when `props` has keys this type doesn't define (typos like `colour`): each names the key and the type's props. The props are kept anyway

overlaps.description: present when a `size: fit` refit covers others, or a `frame` given outright (e.g. a browser tile widened to a desktop viewport) makes the object cover one it didn't before (by layout.check's overlap rule; in a batch, only fits, once the whole batch is laid out): the ids of everything it covers. Grow away from neighbours or move it (layout.place) rather than leave the user's tiles buried

object.upsert.description: Create or update by key, so a script that rebuilds part of the board (a region per ticket) can run again and again without keeping ids: when an object on the board holds `key` it is updated (`props` shallow-merged, `frame` and `size` as object.update; its type must be `type`, else `conflict`), else one is created as object.create would with `key` added to its props. Either way the result names the object's id; `created` says which happened. In object.batch, later ops can name it as "$n" either way, and an upsert of a key an earlier op of the batch creates updates that one.

props.description: the type's props, as for object.create (on an update, merged into the object's)

frame.description: as for object.create; on an update, as object.update's (any of x, y, w, h). Omit it to leave where the object is (a region the user moved stays moved)

expires.description: RFC3339 timestamp with timezone, or null to clear; omission preserves an existing deadline; mutually exclusive with expiresIn

expiresIn.description: finite nonnegative duration (s, m, h, d; fractions allowed), resolved once by the host to absolute expires; mutually exclusive with expires

created.description: true: nothing held the key, so the object is new

object.delete.description: Delete an object (and remove it from any staged mentions). Arrows bound to it keep their drawn route: that end becomes a free `point` where it last attached.

viewer.description: With step, record this remote window's edit for board.undo. Both fields are required together and forbidden inside object.batch.

step.description: The viewer's gesture id; writes with the same id form one undo step.

object.measure.description: Intrinsic size: the whole frame (tile title bar included, exactly the box the tile draws) that shows the content without scrolling. code: exactly `range` (or the symbol, or the whole file), as wide as its longest line up to `width` (default 1546, 200 columns) with longer lines soft-wrapped and counted in the height, with the caption strip when `caption` is set, and wide enough for the whole caption up to that same maximum (a longer caption truncates); note: the rendered markdown (live fences resolved) at `width` (default 280); shape: text at `width` (default one unwrapped line per paragraph), rect/ellipse around their text; html: `width` wide (default 640) and as tall as the page's document laid out at that width, once it has rendered (Mermaid, excerpts), at most 4000 (a longer page scrolls; layout.check reports the rest); changes: the file list and every file and hunk row under its header (deleted and viewed files folded, as the tile starts), as wide as the longest line up to `width` (default 960, at least 480), longer lines wrapped, at most 4000 tall; image: its picture at one point per pixel, at most `width` (default 960) wide, plus the caption strip (`not_found` when the file isn't a readable image). A tile with `zoom` lays out at `width` ÷ zoom, and its frame is the 26-pt title bar plus that body times zoom (as wide as its natural width times zoom). Other types are `unsupported`.

props.description: the type's props: TerminalProps, BrowserProps, CodeProps, NoteProps, HtmlProps, ChangesProps, ImageProps, VideoProps, DiagramProps, QuestionProps, ShapeProps, ArrowProps, or GroupProps (`easl methods <Name>` lists one). `scale` is invalid_params (a tile's content zoom is `zoom`, a text shape's font `textSize`)

width.description: wrap width for notes and text; maximum width for code (default 1546, 200 columns), images and video (default 960); the width an html page lays out at (default 640)

approximate.description: the size uses easld's glyph-table text approximation or a client's fallback HTML layout, rather than exact Mac layout. Absent when exact. easld itself has no fallback HTML layout engine

object.reload.description: Load a browser tile's page again, as its reload button does (the same address, Back history untouched; a failed load is retried): any browser tile, including one the user or `object.create` made. Waits until the page has loaded or `timeoutMs` passes, so an `easl get <tile> --since <cursor>` right after reads the new page's log (`reloaded: true`). The page changes that follow are credited to `caller` in `board.history`. A calls diagram tile is computed again from the code (its nodes re-resolved by symbol; gone ones badged stale), waiting up to `timeoutMs` (default 60000: a language server's first answers in a project take a while); the result counts nodes and names the stale ones, and `object.get` has the graph (`props.graph`). A kind graph diagram reads only `props.knowledge` and reload is a no-op success. Only browser and diagram tiles reload: code, note and changes tiles follow their files by themselves.

timeoutMs.description: how long to wait for the page to finish loading (a diagram: to be computed, default 60000); 0 returns as soon as the reload has started

url.description: browser tiles: the address the page shows

loaded.description: the page finished loading (a diagram: was computed) within `timeoutMs`

root.description: diagram tiles: the root node's id

nodes.description: diagram tiles: nodes in the graph, the root and stale ones included

stale.description: diagram tiles: ids of nodes whose symbol is gone

error.description: diagram tiles: why the graph couldn't be computed (it keeps the last good one)

failed.description: the page couldn't load: why, in a few words ("connection refused"); the tile shows it and retries a local address itself

object.batch.description: Apply several changes atomically: one board revision and one undo step, and if any op fails nothing changes (the error names the op). Ops are object.create/update/upsert/delete and layout.place/stack/translate/grid with their usual params; the string "$n" anywhere in an op's params stands for the id op n created (or, an upsert, created or updated) (e.g. an arrow from "$0" to "$1", a group with members ["$0", "$1"], a grid cell {"id": "$2", "row": 0, "col": 1}).

layout.place.description: Move an object `gap` points beside another (one undo step). Groups move their members; arrows follow their bound ends.

align.description: along the side: start lines up top (or left) edges, end bottom (or right) edges

layout.stack.description: Lay objects out in a row (left to right) or column (top to bottom), `gap` apart, starting where the first one is or at `origin` (one undo step). With `wrapAt`, a line longer than that many points wraps into a new line. Groups move as a whole, so stacking groups lays out lanes.

align.description: across the line: rows align tops (start), middles, or bottoms

layout.translate.description: Move objects by (dx, dy) in one undo step. Groups move with their members (a member listed beside its group moves once), arrows carry their free ends, and arrows bound to moved objects follow. For build-offscreen-then-swap: create a layout far away in a batch, then translate it into place.

layout.grid.description: Place objects in shared columns and rows (one undo step): a column is as wide as its widest cell and a row as tall as its tallest, measured from the cells' current frames, `colGap`/`rowGap` apart, so columns line up across rows even when the cells belong to different groups (their groups re-fit). Row and column numbers only order cells; unused numbers take no space. Groups as cells move whole. Leave `rowGap` room for group padding and title bands between rows of different groups.

colAlign.description: across the column: left edges (start), centers, or right edges line up

rowAlign.description: down the row: top edges (start), middles, or bottom edges line up

origin.description: the grid's top-left; default the cells' current top-left

layout.check.description: Layout problems for `ids`, for what intersects `rect`, or for the whole board, judged by what is drawn (a tile's frame is its whole box, title bar included; arrows route as drawn, line-bound ends at their lines): overlapping objects (a group and its members don't count; unfilled rects/ellipses are annotations and never overlap anything), arrows whose route runs through tiles, text, or filled shapes other than their own ends, arrow labels lying on a tile, text, or filled shape (their own ends included), a group's title, another label, or another arrow's line, arrows drawn on top of each other (`arrowOverlaps`: shared length) or crossing each other (`arrowIntersections`), note/text/html whose content doesn't fit its frame (`overflow`: points missing in x and y; html: its page's document laid out at the frame's width), code tiles whose range's rows are taller than the frame (`scrolls`: the tile scrolls to its range, fine for a viewer meant to scroll; refit with `size: "fit"` when the whole range should show), and code captions or note tables cut off by the frame (`truncated`; a note's table cells wrap within its width, so only a table with too many columns for it is cut). Follow tiles are fixed-size viewers and never count as overflow or truncated.

frame.description: where the label chip is drawn (an arrow's own frame leaves it out)

overlaps.description: objects under the label; an arrow id means that arrow's label, a group id that group's title

lines.description: other arrows whose line runs under the label

arrowOverlaps.description: pairs of arrows drawn on top of each other (collinear within 3 points): readers can't tell them apart there

at.description: the middle of the first shared run

arrowIntersections.description: pairs of arrows whose lines cross; fewer read better, and moving a tile or reordering a column often removes them

scrolls.description: code tiles whose range's rows (wrapped at the frame's width) are `y` points taller than the frame: they scroll to the range

truncated.description: text the frame's width cuts off with "…": a code tile's caption, or a note's table with more columns than the note has room for even with its cells wrapped

x.description: points of width missing to show all of it

hints.description: present when there is advice that isn't a fault: more than 6 labelled arrows all one color (label chips are outlined in their arrow's color, so one color can't show which line a label names): color arrows by lane or flow

approximate.description: an `overflow`, `truncated` or `labelOverlaps` finding rests on a text size from easld's glyph table (no attached Mac client measured it): check it by eye. A finding exact sizes would add isn't flagged

tray.list.description: Staged mentions, in staging order. On an app-local remote tab this is the viewer's private tray, never the host user's tray.

tray.stage.description: Stage a mention (normally done by the user with Hyper-click; exposed for tests and agents). An app-local remote board target stages in this viewer's private tray.

tray.unstage.description: Remove one staged mention from this app's local board or remote viewer tray, never another user's tray.

tray.drain.description: Resolve all staged mentions at their current revision and return them with a ready-to-inject context block. By default the tray is cleared; with `peek: true` it is left intact so the caller can `tray.commit` exactly these ids once the context has really been delivered (a cancelled prompt then loses nothing). The tray's mentions are for the terminal it shows (the board's prompt target, `view.get` `promptTarget`): a `caller` tile that isn't that terminal gets none of them, the tray stays as it is, and `held` says how many wait for `target`. Without a caller (a script) or while the board has no window, the tray drains to anyone. A `caller` also gets the mentions other agents attached for it with `agent.prompt` `mentions` (never shown in the tray), after the tray's, in a block per sending terminal (`<canvas-mentions … from="obj_…">` and a line naming it); `tray.commit` of their ids removes them too. In the context, a mention of the caller's own terminal says `(your terminal)`; other terminals are named (their `name`, else title). `prompt` is the text the caller's agent integration is about to submit (its submission drain, the text as the agent passes it). Compared folded (letters and digits only, case-folded), so an agent's rewrites don't matter: when it contains the text of a prompt the user sent the caller from easl's composer with mentions (the oldest such; a folded text under 3 characters must equal it), the drain is that prompt's and takes the mentions it carried (numbered from 1) instead of the tray (`tray.commit` of their ids ends the wait). An answer Codex submits as a prompt is matched the same way and takes nothing. Any other drain takes the tray as described.

board.description: an app-local remote board target drains only this viewer's private tray, never the host user's tray

prompt.description: the prompt text being submitted, in an agent integration's submission drain: compared folded (letters and digits only, case-folded) with the prompts easl's composer typed into the caller

context.description: ready-to-inject prompt context: the tray's block, then one block per agent that attached mentions for the caller; empty string when there is nothing for the caller

held.description: present when the caller isn't the terminal the tray shows: the mentions left staged for it

target.description: with `held`: the terminal the tray shows, if any

tray.commit.description: Remove exactly these mentions from the tray after their context was delivered (second half of a `peek` drain). Unknown ids are ignored. On an app-local remote tab only this viewer's private tray changes.

agent.report.description: Report lifecycle state for the agent running in a terminal tile. Stale `seq` values from the same source are ignored. With `call`, `blocked` means that tool call waits for the user's approval and `working` that it finished: while any reported call waits, the tile stays `blocked` (with the oldest waiting call's message) whatever other calls finish; finishing it re-raises the next one. With `serial`, a `blocked` call replaces every earlier wait (agents that ask one approval at a time), so the message always names the request on screen. `working` without `call` (a new prompt) and `idle` end every wait. `unknown`: an agent without a lifecycle integration runs in the tile (a wrapper such as `bin/aider` reports it as the agent starts): the tile counts as an agent for the tray and `agent.wait`, and its terminal notifications report when it waits (lifecycle `via: "notifications"`).

call.description: identifies the tool call the report is about, the same for its approval request and its completion (the hooks hash the tool and its input)

final.description: only with `idle`: the final assistant message of the turn that just ended (the text `agent.read` `final` returns until the next turn starts)

serial.description: with `blocked` and `call`: the agent asks one approval at a time (Codex), so this request ends every earlier wait (an approval answered whose completion never matched or hasn't arrived yet)

error.description: only with `idle`: the turn ended on this error instead of finishing (an API error such as `overloaded_error`, an abort, the output token limit). The tile goes `idle` with it as its message and as its lifecycle's `error`, never `done`, until a turn starts (also through agent.restart), and `agent.read` `final` reports the answer as cut off (`cutOff`)

protocol.description: the integration protocol version (kept as `props.agent.protocol`; every report says it, a report without it means 0). 1: the integration takes out-of-band messages (agent.inbox), so agent.prompt queues for it instead of typing into the terminal

draft.description: the agent's input editor holds text the user hasn't sent (kept as `props.agent.draft`; every report of an integration that tracks it says it, a report without it means unknown). agent.restart refuses unless it is false. omp's extension reports it when the editor goes from empty to holding text and back, whether the user typed it or omp put it there (a restored draft)

pid.description: the agent's process id (kept as `props.agent.pid`; a report without it forgets it): agent.list `pid`

agent.report_session.description: Report the agent's native session identity so the tile can resume it after a reboot, and the model and thinking level it runs, which agent.restart relaunches it with. Report again when either changes; a field left out keeps its last value. Another session where one was recorded (a new conversation, or another agent) ends the one before: the messages still queued for it bounce (agent.inbox).

model.description: the model, as the agent's own `--model` takes it (omp: `provider/id`)

thinking.description: the thinking level, as the agent's own option takes it (omp `--thinking`: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, auto)

agent.release.description: The agent in this tile exited; clear its lifecycle authority and its recorded session (`agent.report_session`), so after a reboot the tile runs its `command` (a plain shell when it has none) instead of resuming that session. The messages its integration never took bounce (agent.inbox).

agent.list.description: Every terminal tile on every board easl has stored, open or not, with the agent in it: a terminal whose agent never reported (a shell, a CLI without easl hooks) has kind and lifecycle `unknown`. An agent without an integration that sends terminal notifications (aider through easl's `aider` wrapper, any CLI's OSC 9/777 or bell) is listed with its program as `kind` and a lifecycle `via: "notifications"`: `done` when it last said it waits, `unknown` after a prompt until it says so again, never `working` or `blocked`. A closed board's tiles come from its saved board file (`open: false`, lifecycle as saved) with `live` from the zmx sessions labelled for them: an agent there keeps running while its board is closed, but nothing hears its reports until the board opens again, and agent.prompt, agent.wait, agent.read and agent.restart reach only open boards. Open boards' tiles come first, each board's sorted by tile id, then closed boards' by board id.

agent.prompt.description: Prompt another agent. To a terminal whose integration takes messages (agent.report `protocol` ≥ 1: omp's extension) the text goes out of band: it is queued for that terminal and its integration delivers it as a message (agent.inbox), never touching the terminal, so a half-typed draft, an open question or an approval dialog stays as it is. The receiver gets a header naming the sender and how to reply (`write agent://<address>` in omp, `easl tell <address>`). `when: "now"` (the default): a working agent gets it as a steer (at its next step; a wait is cut short), an idle one starts a turn with it, one waiting on a question or approval gets it after the answer. `when: "next-turn"`: never into a running turn; it starts a turn once the running one has ended. Messages arriving together are delivered as one, and each sender wakes a receiver at most 20 times an hour (past that, messages wait for its next turn). A message from a terminal (`caller`) is attributed to an agent; one from a script (`from`, or no `caller`) to the user, named by `from`. A message is for the agent session there as it is sent: when that session ends before its integration takes the message (the agent released, exited, or replaced by another session), the message bounces, back to a sending terminal whose integration takes messages as a message from `easl` (`undelivered to <address>: <its first line>…`), else into the receiver's board.history (`message`); a session that ends while the message is being sent fails the call `unavailable`, and so does a target whose message integration died without releasing its terminal (killed: its shell is back at the prompt), typed or not. Any other target gets the text typed: pasted (bracketed paste; a one-line command into a shell at its prompt is typed) and Enter pressed once the paste has landed (80 ms later: TUIs such as Gemini CLI take an Enter right after input as part of it); the composer always types. The terminal's text just before submitting (or queueing) is remembered, so `agent.read` with `since: "prompt"` returns only what followed. `agent.wait` after it ignores the state the agent was in before this prompt: it answers once the agent has reported `working` (or `blocked`) and then reached one of its `until` states, so wait for `done` right away, not for `working` first; while a message waits to be delivered it doesn't answer at all. A prompt that lands while the agent is `working` (typed, or a `now` message delivered as a steer) joins that turn (omp and Codex take it before the turn ends and answer it in the same turn): the wait answers when that turn ends, and `final` is that turn's answer. For typing only: a `blocked` target fails with `conflict` naming what it waits on (an approval dialog or question would take the text) unless `force` is true. So does a `working` target whose state is `restored` (from before the app last closed, unconfirmed since: it may wait on a question now). So does a target whose agent reports from behind another foreground program (`program` nvim, less: the text would go to that program), and one in tmux whose active pane runs something else (vim, a shell): the text goes to the active pane, so it is sent when that pane runs the agent. A typed `next-turn` prompt to a `working` target fails with `conflict` (typed text would join the turn). Into a shell at its prompt (no agent), a one-line text is typed rather than pasted. `mentions` attach board objects for the receiving agent the way the user's Hyper-click mentions do: they wait for that terminal only (never in the user's tray) and arrive resolved, as hidden context with a typed prompt (its integration's next submitted prompt, this one) or with the message, in a block naming your terminal (`caller`). The target must run an agent with an easl integration (its lifecycle not `via: "notifications"`), else `unavailable`. An agent reporting by notification goes `unknown` with this prompt, and `agent.wait` answers at its next notification (none comes when the text needed no model reply, e.g. aider's `/add`: give such waits a `timeoutMs`).

target.description: a tile id, `name` or `name@board` (the board's name is its root folder's name): a bare name is looked up on the caller's board first, then on every open board; more than one match is `ambiguous`

mentions.description: objects on the target's board to attach, e.g. [{"object": "obj_…"}, {"object": "obj_…", "lines": {"start": 41, "end": 48}}]

staged.description: With composer only, complete staged mentions in token order, copied into that terminal's own prompt queue and numbered from 1. Requires viewer when nonempty. Cannot accompany mentions or answer.

viewer.description: With composer only, the submitting window that receives undelivered staged mentions through composer.returned.

caller.description: the prompting terminal: the sender a message names (its address for replies, resolved at delivery), and whose board a bare `target` name is looked up on first; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

from.description: a sender label for a caller with no tile (a script, a launchd job): `machine-watch`. The message is then the user's (attribution `user`), names this label and has no reply address, even when a `caller` is given (clients fill it inside a terminal; it still decides which board a bare `target` is looked up on first)

when.description: now: a steer into the running turn, or a new turn when idle; next-turn: never into a running turn, delivered once it has ended

message.description: out-of-band only: the id the message gets (`msg_` and 8 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`), the same on every attempt to send it. A prompt whose `message` is already queued for the target answers with that message (`duplicate: true`) and queues nothing, also when the first attempt is still being sent, so a sender whose call timed out can send again without the target getting it twice (a terminal on another machine has its text read over ssh before the message is queued, which can outlast a short timeout). The receiving integration drops an id it already delivered. Typing ignores it

force.description: typing only: send even though the target is `blocked` or runs another foreground program than its agent (e.g. Claude Code or Gemini CLI stays blocked after the user pressed Esc on or denied an approval, since they run no hook then). It types into whatever dialog is open and presses Return, which in an approval menu picks the highlighted option (usually allow): never force an answer to an approval

composer.description: The user's own prompt from a remote composer's window: typed into the terminal even when its integration takes peer messages. Full staged mentions wait for this prompt's matching submission drain, numbered from 1, never the tray or a hand-off. Takes no caller, from, when, force or mentions.

id.description: Client-generated identity, unchanged across attempts at this exact prompt.

epoch.description: The host's agent.prompt_epoch promptEpoch before the first attempt.

createdAt.description: Client creation time. Receipts live for 24 hours. More than five minutes in the future, an expired receipt, or a different epoch cannot authorize execution.

submission.description: An idempotent prompt submission. The host reserves its identity before any asynchronous work and remembers its exact payload and outcome for 24 hours. Reuse with changed parameters is invalid_params. Up to 4096 live receipts are held without evicting an unfinished submission.

reconcile.description: Requires submission. Read its receipt without submitting anything. An absent, unexpired identity in the same epoch is atomically cancelled and returns not-delivered, preventing a late original request from typing. A known outcome is replayed. pending means the first attempt is unfinished; unknown means the host cannot prove whether it reached the terminal. Neither permits restoring an unsent draft or sending again.

answer.description: with `composer`: the text is the user's answer to the question or approval the target is blocked on, so it passes the blocked check (only the user answers; `force` is for agents and scripts). Takes no mentions

agent.description: as it was when the prompt was submitted (its lifecycle is still the previous turn's)

submittedAt.description: when it was typed, or queued as a message

delivery.description: message: queued for the integration; typed: submitted to the terminal. These carry agent, submittedAt and waitable. Receipt states: pending is still in progress; not-delivered is definitively cancelled or refused before execution; unknown must never be retried or restored as an unsent draft.

error.description: With receipt delivery not-delivered: the original definite refusal. An API error to a receipt query is not proof of non-delivery.

message.description: with delivery `message`: the queued message's id

waitable.description: the agent reports a lifecycle (an integration, or by notification), so `agent.wait` can tell when this prompt is done; false: it reports none (yet) and `agent.wait` fails unless a first report arrives within 15 s, so poll `agent.read` with `since: "prompt"`

mentions.description: present with `mentions`: what waits for the target's prompt (an object already waiting there is not attached twice)

duplicate.description: the prompt's `message` was already queued for the target: this is that message, and nothing new was queued

agent.wait.description: Wait until the target agent reaches one of the given states. After `agent.prompt` it waits for that prompt's turn (see agent.prompt); one that starts no turn within 60 s (its agent reports neither `working` nor `blocked`: a `/` command or `!` escape is no turn) fails it with `unavailable`, so read what followed with `agent.read` `since: "prompt"`. A terminal whose lifecycle is `unknown` gets 15 s for a first report (an agent just launched in it) and then fails with `unavailable`, as does one whose agent exits, unless `until` includes `unknown`; an agent reporting by notification (lifecycle `via: "notifications"`) waits for its next notification instead. A read: when the connection drops mid-wait (the app restarts), clients re-send it once the app is back, with `timeoutMs` reduced by the time already waited.

target.description: a tile id, `name` or `name@board`, as agent.prompt's

caller.description: the asking terminal, whose board a bare `target` name is looked up on first; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

agent.read.description: Recent text of an agent's terminal: the tail of its zmx session scrollback as plain text (what the screen shows plus history), trailing blank lines removed. Rows the terminal soft-wrapped read as one line: on the live screen by the terminal's own wrap flags; above it (where the history carries none) a row that fills the terminal's width and ends in text joins the next, unless it is a separator padded to the width, such as pytest's `==== FAILURES ====`, or the next row starts with the same word (pytest's `FAILED …` rows, cut at the width). Inline images (kitty graphics placeholders) read as one `[image]` line. With `block`: the output of a command the terminal's shell finished (`"last"` or -1, -2 the one before; from Ghostty's shell-integration prompt marks and the commands easl saw finish since it attached), with `command` saying what ran; a command-block mention names the `block` that reads it whole. With `final: true`, instead the agent's last answer: the final assistant message of its last finished turn, as its integration reported it (omp, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI; not opencode). It fails with `unavailable` while the agent is in a turn (or hasn't started the one `agent.prompt` sent), and when none is known: never reported, or the turn was interrupted. Answers are saved with the board, so they outlast a restart.

target.description: a tile id, `name` or `name@board`, as agent.prompt's

caller.description: the asking terminal, whose board a bare `target` name is looked up on first; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

lines.description: tail length; larger values are capped at 2000. With `since`: the last this many lines of the reply (default 2000)

since.description: only what the terminal printed after the last `agent.prompt` to it (from the first line that changed since then: the prompt's echo, then the reply and whatever the screen shows below it); `not_found` when no agent.prompt reached it since the app started

block.description: the output of a command the shell finished instead of the tail (its last `lines` lines, default 2000): `"last"` or -1 the last one, -2 the one before, back to the oldest easl saw finish since it attached to the session (`not_found` past it); `unavailable` when there is none (no shell integration) or its rows are gone (cleared, trimmed from the scrollback, reflowed by a width change). Doesn't combine with `since` or `final`

final.description: the last answer instead of the screen; takes no `lines`, `since` or `block`

truncated.description: with `since`: the reply has more lines than returned; with `block`: the output has

command.description: with `block`: the command whose output this is

cutOff.description: with `final`: the turn ended on this error (its agent reported it), so `text` is the answer as far as it got

agent.inbox.description: A terminal's agent integration takes the messages queued for it (agent.prompt to a target whose integration reports `protocol` ≥ 1) and delivers them to its agent, without touching the terminal. `ack` first drops the messages it delivered (`started`: that delivery started a new turn, so agent.wait now waits for that turn as after a prompt to an idle agent; otherwise it joined the running turn). Then it answers the messages waiting that no open connection holds, oldest first, each sender's name and each message's mentions resolved now; they are held by this connection until it acks them or closes, and offered again then. With `waitMs`, when none waits, it answers as soon as one arrives (at most that long, then with none). An integration acks a message once its agent has recorded it, never before, and dedupes by id (one comes again after a lost connection or a restart). Messages are saved with the board, so an app restart keeps them; when the agent session they were queued for ends first (agent.release, its integration dying, another session reported, the terminal deleted) they bounce, as agent.prompt says.

ack.description: messages this integration has handed to its agent

started.description: with `ack`: their delivery started a new turn (the agent was idle), rather than joining the running one

waitMs.description: wait this long for a message when none waits

agent.restart.description: Relaunch the agent in a terminal tile in place: the tile keeps its id, name, frame, and its agent's recorded model and thinking level (agent.report_session `model`, `thinking`). Its zmx session is killed (the agent and everything it started end) and a new session runs the relaunched command; a hosted terminal's (`props.host`) on its host, through that host's easld (`session.kill`, `session.spawn`), `unavailable` while easl isn't connected to it. `resume`: the tile's agent reopens its recorded session (omp `--resume=<session path>`, claude `--resume <id>`, codex `resume <id>`, gemini `--resume <id>`, opencode `--session <id>`), with the options of the tile's `command` when it runs that agent, and the recorded model and thinking (omp `--model=<model> --thinking=<level>`; they replace any the command gave); `unavailable` when no session is recorded (its agent never reported one, or it exited). `fresh`: the same command, model and thinking without a session (a session selector or prompt the command had is left out); a terminal with no recorded agent reruns its `command`. `args` are appended either way. Refused with `conflict` while another restart of the terminal runs or a prompt is being pasted into it (even with `force`: it would land in the relaunched agent), and unless `force` while the agent is `working` (restored or not) or `blocked`, has a prompt whose turn hasn't started (typed, or a message its integration delivered, within agent.wait's grace for it), has a message queued that its integration hasn't taken yet (agent.wait waits for it too; a forced restart bounces it), may hold a draft (agent.list `draft` true, or absent: its integration doesn't say), or the terminal has keyboard focus (agent.list `focused`: the user may be typing in it); checked again just before the kill. While it runs nothing else reaches the terminal: agent.prompt to it fails with `conflict`, and agent.inbox offers it nothing; a typed prompt whose agent session ended before its paste (the restart came while it read the screen) types nothing and fails `unavailable`. Nothing is relaunched until the old session is confirmed gone: when it can't be (another easl instance owns it, or it is still listed 3 s after the kill), `unavailable`, with the session, its agent and its queue as they were; a tile closed while its session is killed is `not_found`, with nothing relaunched. Killing the agent ends its session (agent.inbox): in either mode the messages still queued for it bounce, and none reaches the relaunched agent. The tile's `command` becomes the relaunched one without its session selector, so a reboot relaunches the same agent; its lifecycle is cleared (`unknown`) until the new agent reports, so agent.wait gives it 15 s for a first report. A `done` the user hasn't seen (the needs-you badge) stays instead, through the relaunched agent's reports that start no turn, until the user sees the tile or the relaunched agent starts one (`working`); so does a turn that ended on an error (lifecycle `error`), seen or not, until the relaunched agent starts a turn; agent.wait still waits for the relaunched agent's first report. Only tiles of open boards; a remote board's terminal is its host's to restart, through the host's API.

target.description: a tile id, `name` or `name@board`, as agent.prompt's

caller.description: the asking terminal, whose board a bare `target` name is looked up on first; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

mode.description: resume: reopen the recorded session; fresh: a new session with the same command, model and thinking

args.description: arguments appended to the relaunched command, e.g. ["--plan"]

force.description: restart even though the agent is working or blocked, has a prompt whose turn hasn't started or a message queued it hasn't taken, the user is in the terminal, or its editor holds a draft (or may: its integration doesn't say): that work, prompt, dialog or draft is lost, and the queued messages bounce. Never past another restart of the terminal or a prompt being pasted into it

agent.description: the tile as relaunched: lifecycle `unknown` until its new agent reports, or the `done` the user hasn't seen, or the `idle` of a turn that ended on an error (`error`)

command.description: the argv the new session runs

follow.report.description: Report a file location an agent just read, edited, or wrote; re-aims that terminal's follow tile, creating it in a free spot near the terminal (unless the user is working in it, which holds re-aims for ~10 s). Ignored while the terminal's `props.follow` is false, and for files outside the board root, the terminal's cwd, and the other worktrees of their repositories (a worktree file keeps its absolute path and its own gutter), scratch files in the temp directory, missing files, images, PDFs, archives, and other binaries: the tile keeps its last real file.

path.description: absolute path or path relative to the board root

range.description: where to aim; omitted with `changes`, the hunk spanning the most lines (the last of equals)

changes.description: an edit's hunks as lines of the file now (a deletion: the line after it); the tile flashes them all

view.seen.description: Acknowledge what a viewer saw without rewriting lifecycle props. A marker clears only when its raisedAt still matches marker; a terminal is marked seen only when its current revision equals rev. Working or blocked terminals are never marked seen. Stale acknowledgments leave newer markers and answers unchanged.

object.description: The canonical terminal after an accepted seen acknowledgment whose supplied rev matched its pre-acknowledgment revision. Omitted for stale revisions, missing revisions, marker-only acknowledgments, and rejected seen acknowledgments.

view.attention.description: Raise an attention marker pointing at an object (one per object; raising again replaces its message), or remove it with `clear: true`. A marker belongs to the caller's turn: raising one clears the markers the same caller raised in earlier turns (a turn starts when its lifecycle goes to working from idle, done, or no state; answering an approval, blocked → working, continues the turn); markers from this turn stay. The user seeing the object also clears it. Unseen markers are stored with the board and survive app restarts; deleting the object removes its marker. Never moves the user's viewport.

clear.description: remove this object's marker instead of raising it

caller.description: the raising agent's terminal; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

id.description: the marked object (markers are keyed by object)

active.description: a marker is showing after this call

cleared.description: present when raising cleared the caller's markers from earlier turns: their objects

view.get.description: What the user is looking at right now, without pixels: the visible board rect and zoom, the prompt-target terminal, the tile with keyboard focus, the selection, whether the window is visible on screen, and its appearance (dark or light).

board.description: an open local board id or the host board id from a remote board.list row. Remote tabs return this app's viewer state, not the host's window state. Open and stored local ids, including migrated ids, take precedence; a closed local target remains not_found. Several matching remote tabs are ambiguous

promptTarget.description: terminal that receives the tray and dictation

visible.description: the window is at least partly visible on a displayed Space

appearance.description: the window's appearance, which tiles and renders draw in: match charts and pages to it (dark: transparent or dark backgrounds, light text)

view.open_url.description: Open a web address the way a ⌘-click on it in the caller's terminal does: an http or https URL shows in a browser tile beside the caller, and a tile already showing that address (compared by scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment, so `HTTP://Example.com:80` is `http://example.com/`) is reused (`existing: true`) instead of a duplicate. The user's view pans the least that shows the tile, never so far that the caller's terminal leaves view. Keyboard focus stays where it was: the tile is selected unless that would take the keyboard from another tile than a terminal (a note being edited, a page or code rows being typed in), which keeps it and its selection. Anything but http(s) is `invalid_params`: hand other schemes to the system (`/usr/bin/open`). The `bin/open` shim and `$BROWSER` in a terminal tile call this.

url.description: an absolute http or https URL

board.description: an open local board id. An app-local remote tab target is unsupported because forwarding would move the host user's viewport. Use the remote tab's native link action or connect directly to its host

caller.description: the terminal the link comes from: the tile opens beside it; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

object.description: the browser tile showing the address

existing.description: a tile already showed the address: nothing was created

view.render.description: Render part of the board offscreen at a fixed scale, independent of the user's viewport (never moves it). `target` is an object id, a list of ids, or a board rect; ids render the board region under their outlines (with whatever overlaps them) and the whole route of every arrow between two of them, `full` draws those tiles' whole content (note/HTML scroll height; code: all of its range, scrolled to it and wrapped at its tile's width) extending below/right of their frames. Waits until content has painted (up to `timeoutMs`) and reports per-object state instead of returning blanks. App chrome (toolbar, tray, hints, selection rings, attention markers) is never drawn. A tile draws as on screen: its title bar at 1× (showing its content zoom's % when not 100%), its content at its `zoom` inside the frame.

board.description: an open local board id or the host board id of an open remote tab. Remote tabs render this app's viewer content and require inline:true without out, so host content is not written locally. Open and stored local ids, including migrated ids, take precedence; a closed local target remains not_found. Several matching remote tabs are ambiguous

scale.description: pixels per board point; lowered to keep the image under 32 megapixels (the result says what was used)

full.description: id targets: render the whole content, not just the part inside the frame

exclude.description: object types and/or object ids to leave out (e.g. ["terminal", "obj_…"]); a group id takes its members with it; targets are always drawn

padding.description: board points added around the target

out.description: absolute path to write; format from the extension (.png, .jpg/.jpeg). Clients resolve relative paths. Omitted: a new file under $TMPDIR/easl-renders/ (out of the repo)

inline.description: return the image in the reply (`data`, base64) and write no file: for a client on another machine, such as a remote board's viewer, which can't read the host's files. Doesn't combine with `out`

format.description: format of the temporary file, or of `data` with `inline`, when no `out` is given

timeoutMs.description: how long to wait for content (HTML pages, browser pages including loading one that isn't loaded, file reads) before drawing placeholders

path.description: absolute path written: `out`, or the temporary file; absent with `inline`

canvasRect.description: board area the image covers: pixel (px, py) = board (x + px / scale, y + py / scale)

scale.description: pixels per board point actually used

objects.description: every object drawn, bottom to top

view.snapshot.description: The board's window as the user sees it right now (viewport, tiles, toolbar, tray), with the viewport it shows. Terminal tiles are drawn from their session text. To look at something regardless of where the user is, use view.render.

board.description: an open local board id. An app-local remote tab target is unsupported because snapshots would persist host content locally; use view.render with inline:true instead

out.description: absolute path to write; format from the extension (.png, .jpg/.jpeg). Clients resolve relative paths. Omitted: a new file under $TMPDIR/easl-renders/ (out of the repo)

format.description: format of the temporary file when no `out` is given

path.description: absolute path written: `out`, or the temporary file

scale.description: image pixels per board point (backing scale × zoom); the board fills the image from its top-left: pixel (px, py) = board (viewport.rect.x + px / scale, viewport.rect.y + py / scale)

objects.description: objects at least partly visible, bottom to top (state is always rendered)

session.spawn.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): start terminal tile `tile`'s zmx session, `canvas-<tile>`, on the machine easld runs on, as easld's own child, so the session and everything it runs stay in easld's cgroup (a hosted terminal's session: docs/contracts.md "Hosted terminals"). `command` runs in the user's login shell, which stays when it exits (`$SHELL -l -c '<command>; exec $SHELL -l'`); without one the session is the login shell. zmx keeps its sockets and logs in `<easld home>/zmx`, the user's own (a symlink, another user's directory or one others can write to is `unavailable`). A session that exists already is left as it is (`created: false`), unless one of its `canvas.home`, `canvas.board` and `canvas.tile` labels isn't the one `labels` gives (`conflict`, naming it). Its `canvas.board` may also be one of `merged`, the board ids the caller's board took in; its home and tile must still match. zmx's dead sessions (`status=cleaning up`) don't exist. Clients attach to it with `zmx attach canvas-<tile>` in that directory, once they have checked its labels.

tile.description: the terminal tile: the session is `canvas-<tile>`

command.description: argv run in the login shell; absent or empty: just the login shell

cwd.description: an existing directory on easld's machine (default: the user's home)

env.description: variables the session gets over easld's own environment (`EASL_SOCKET`, `EASL_TILE_ID`, `EASL_BOARD_ID`, …); `PATH` goes before easld's own

labels.description: zmx labels the session is created with (`canvas.board`, `canvas.tile`, `canvas.home`); keys and values in [A-Za-z0-9._-]

merged.description: board ids the caller's board took in (`repo.merged`): an existing session labelled with one of them is accepted when its home and tile labels match. The session keeps its original labels. Absent or empty: only the board label in `labels` matches

created.description: false: the session was already running

session.list.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): the terminal tiles' zmx sessions on easld's machine (`canvas-…`, whoever started them).

pid.description: the session's process (zmx's), absent while it doesn't answer

unreachable.description: zmx lists the session but it doesn't answer (its daemon stopped or wedged)

session.kill.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): end terminal tile `tile`'s zmx session on easld's machine and delete zmx's log of it. A session not labelled with `home` is left alone (`conflict`).

home.description: the caller's `canvas.home` label: only a session with this one is ended (without `home`, any)

killed.description: false: there was no such session

relay.open.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): serve a client's sockets to the programs on easld's machine, so a hosted terminal's integration and the `easl` CLI there reach the board that shows it (docs/contracts.md "Hosted terminals"). easld listens on `<home>/run/<instance>/easl.sock` and `cmux.sock` (the user's only) and passes each connection on to `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the client's ssh forward of a loopback port back to itself. Every user of the machine can reach that port, and anyone can listen on it once the forward is gone, so neither end sends the token: easld sends `<socket name> <nonce>`, the client's end answers `<nonce> <proof>` and easld `<proof>`, each proof the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the token, of `easl-relay <gate|easld> <socket name> <easld's nonce> <the client's nonce>`; nothing passes until both check. A connection the client's end doesn't take (refused, or no proof) closes at once, the integration spooling its report, and disarms the relay until the client opens it again. Opening it again with the same token takes the port; with a new one (the client's app restarted, or it reconnected) the sockets are bound anew at the same paths, so integrations watching them report again.

instance.description: the client instance, [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 64 characters

port.description: the loopback port the client's ssh forwards to it

token.description: 16–128 letters and digits: the secret both ends prove on every connection, new for each of the client's connections

easl.description: the socket for the easl API (a hosted terminal's `EASL_SOCKET`; integrations spool undelivered reports in `agent-reports/` beside it)

cmux.description: the socket for the cmux browser subset (`CMUX_SOCKET_PATH`)

opened.description: reports may have been spooled meanwhile (fetch and replay them): the sockets were bound now, a disarmed relay re-armed, or the first open after easld restored it at startup; false for later opens with the same token and an armed relay

events.subscribe.description: Turn this connection into an event stream. Events: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, tray.changed, agent.lifecycle, follow.updated, attention.changed ({id, active, message?, raisedBy?, raisedAt?}), composer.returned and composer.submitted (ComposerReceipt: {receipt, event, viewer, terminal, ids}, original staged mention ids for the originating viewer, never captured targets), client.changed ({clients}, the current attached-client snapshot for this board; transient, never stored), board.closed and board.opened (BoardLifecycleEvent envelopes with canonical board and empty data). A composer submission receipt follows actual queue consumption, not typing or a peek; board.get replays the newest 2000 receipts after a reconnect. Lifecycle events follow successful close and newly opened board transitions only. Subscriptions stay connected across close and reopen; board and event-name filters apply to lifecycle events as to object events. Private surface.frame, surface.dialog and surface.notice use SurfaceEvent envelopes and are sent only to a stream's owning connection after its matching canonical-board subscription, never broadcast to other board subscribers.

board.description: a board owned by this server; an app-local remote tab target is unsupported. Subscribe on the board host instead

viewer.activity.description: Optional Mac app host report from a remote board viewer on its board event connection. Requires a subscription to object.updated on this open board. input false registers an attached viewer without resetting idle time; true reports actual user input, never background API requests, terminal output or refreshes. A terminal names the tile receiving real keyboard, paste or drop input through its SSH/zmx attachment. Sessions end when the connection, board or terminal ends. Viewers coalesce reports with a trailing report so the final input keeps its full idle-protection window. Unknown-method errors on older servers disable this optional reporting without affecting viewing or input. Not forwarded by easld.

board.description: a board owned by this server; an app-local remote tab target is unsupported. Report on the board host's subscribed connection instead

client.attach.description: Attach this connection as a Mac client serving the named methods and open boards, including background boards. The optional identity is persistent per app home; the returned cli_ id identifies only this connection. Older schema versions are refused unavailable; newer versions speak the server's version, and equal versions work across schema hashes. Unknown attach params and serves names are ignored. Calls normally go to the capable viewer that focused this board last, then focused most recently, then attached last. Browser calls, browser object.reload and view.render targeting one browser instead go only to the tile's persisted drawingMachine identity. A singleton target list also names one browser. Multi-object render lists and rectangles stay on the viewer's compositor, including streamed browsers owned elsewhere. An eligible creator supplies a new browser's default; otherwise the earliest eligible attached Mac supplies it. The first eligible attachment fills existing missing owners. Disconnect never migrates a page. Delegated requests retain their method, with canonical board/target ids. Prompt mentions are queued by easld. HTML measurement receives resolved props and width. Rendering is requested inline without out; only the server writes caller-requested render files. Results and errors otherwise pass through. Reload waits timeoutMs plus 5 s; render waits timeoutMs plus 30 s. Browser wait uses its requested timeout plus grace. Other deadlines are 5 s for view.get, 30 s for view.snapshot, 25 s for HTML object.measure, 10 s for terminal calls and 2 s for text.measure. Missing, disconnected or unresponsive clients fail unavailable, except text.measure falls back to the glyph table. Attach again to replace capabilities, boards or focus; closing detaches. Answer delegated calls without awaiting a new request on this same link, and answer text.measure without any server request because it may hold the board lock.

version.description: the schema `version` the client was built from: older than the server's is refused; a newer client speaks the server's (the reply's `version`)

schema.description: the client's schema hash: the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its schema/easl-api.json (generated: ApiParams.schemaHash)

app.description: the client's easl version, e.g. "0.2.0", for messages

host.description: the machine it runs on, for messages

identity.description: this app home's persistent machine identity, unchanged across reconnects and relaunches; distinct from the connection's cli_ id. Needed to serve browser.call

serves.description: the methods this client answers: view.get, view.render, view.snapshot, agent.prompt, agent.read, agent.restart, object.reload, object.measure, text.measure, browser.call, surface.stream, surface.ack, surface.progress, surface.input, surface.answer, surface.stop (others are ignored)

boards.description: the boards this client serves, in a window, tab, or background attachment, each open on the server; default none

focused.description: the board its user is looking at now (the key window's selected tab), one of `boards`; the client focused last on a board serves that board first

client.list.description: The clients attached to easld, including background viewers. Each entry names its app, host, served boards and methods. Entries, boards and methods are sorted by id or name. The Mac app answers unsupported.

identity.description: the persistent app-home machine identity, absent on older clients; distinct from this connection's id

app.description: the client's easl version, absent when not reported

host.description: the client's machine, absent when not reported

focused.description: the board this client last focused, absent when it never focused

browser.call.description: Run a page-scoped cmux browser command on this browser tile's persisted drawingMachine. Easld forwards only to that attached identity, never to the most recently focused viewer. The drawing Mac uses its own page and profile. Results and errors pass through in memory; no page body, image, cookie or profile is stored by easld. Offline returns unavailable naming the drawing machine. Structural cmux open, list and close stay on easld. The Mac app's host API answers unsupported; its own agents use the cmux socket.

params.description: the cmux command's params, without surface selection; checked by the drawing Mac's existing browser command parser

caller.description: the terminal driving the page, credited for its actions

browser.report.description: A drawing Mac reports committed page URL and title metadata to easld. Only an attached client serving this board whose persistent identity matches the tile's drawingMachine may report. URL commits preserve agent, user or system credit; pageTitle is bookkeeping with no rev bump. No page body, image, cookie, log or profile field is accepted. The Mac app's host API answers unsupported.

pageTitle.description: the page's title; null removes it

caller.description: explicit terminal credit from the drawing Mac, never filled from the reporting process's environment; mutually exclusive with actor

actor.description: URL credit when no caller is given; mutually exclusive with caller

text.measure.description: Sizes of text as the board lays it out, in board points: an attached Mac client that serves text.measure (client.attach) measures it with AppKit, exactly as it draws; with none, or when it doesn't answer within 2 s, the server approximates from its glyph table (advance widths of the app's fonts, extracted on a Mac; no kerning) and says `approximate: true`. object.measure, `size: fit`, layout.check and arrow routing measure through it. note: `text` is markdown laid out as a note `width` wide (default 280) with its live fences and images read under `root`: the size is the note's whole frame (title bar included) and `tableShortfall` how much wider it would have to be to show every table cell whole; text: a text shape's text at `textSize` (default 1: 20 pt Shantell Sans) wrapped at `width` (default unwrapped): its bounds rounded up, plus 2; label: a rect's or ellipse's label (18 pt, centered) wrapped at `width`, likewise; arrowLabel: an arrow's caption (15 pt, centered, wrapped at 240): its chip, 8 wider than the text; caption: a code tile's caption strip (`inline code` in the code font): the narrowest frame that shows it whole, and the strip's height.

width.description: note: the frame's width (default 280); text and label: the wrap width (default unwrapped); ignored by arrowLabel and caption

root.description: note: the directory its fences' and images' paths are read under (default the board root)

board.description: the board whose root a note's paths default to

tableShortfall.description: note: points of width missing to show every table cell whole (0: nothing cut)

approximate.description: measured from the server's glyph table, not by a Mac client
